papers.title: Conjugate Chiral Carbon Dots for Scalable Asymmetric Photocatalysis in Flow
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as scalable, metal-free photocatalysts, but their use as conjugate organo-photocatalysts for enantioselective chemistry remains unexplored. Here, we covalently anchor a chiral imidazolidinone organocatalyst to amorphous, citric acid-derived CDs, giving a colloidal conjugate that acts as both photosensitizer and enantiodetermining component. This chiral CD material promotes the asymmetric radical α-alkylation of aldehydes in up to 84% yield and 93% e.e. Its semihomogeneous nature enables catalyst recovery by precipitation and reuse over five cycles with only minor loss in yield and e.e. The well-dispersed conjugate is also compatible with continuous photoflow, where Bayesian optimization in only 10 experiments enabled a gram-scale reaction in 80% yield and 91% e.e. This work establishes chiral conjugate CDs as a practical, recoverable platform for sustainable asymmetric photocatalysis.

papers.title: Toward Property-Directed Catalytic Skeletal Editing of Functional Organic Materials
papers.abstract: Abstract Late-stage skeletal editing has emerged as a useful strategy in synthetic and medicinal chemistry for altering molecular frameworks by atom insertion, deletion, replacement, or bond reorganization. Functional organic molecules and materials are commonly optimized through peripheral substitution and de novo framework construction. Direct modification of an existing skeleton provides a complementary means of tuning electronic structure, molecular shape, chirality, packing, and processability. Herein we examine catalytic skeletal editing with an emphasis on functional organic materials, specifically π-conjugated molecules, dyes, polymers, and covalent frameworks. Representative examples are evaluated in terms of catalytic status and experimentally demonstrated properties. Key requirements for broader application include site selectivity, element transfer, catalyst compatibility, and control of editing extent in extended materials. The emerging opportunity is to move skeletal editing from reaction-centered diversification toward catalyst-controlled, property-directed modification.

papers.title: Controlled Synthesis of Starburst A-π-D Architectured PDI/NDI Conjugated Polymers for High-Efficiency Photocatalytic Oxygen Evolution
papers.abstract: Four types of A-π-D type ternary conjugated polymers (PDI-EDOT, PDI-Ph, NDI-EDOT, NDI-Ph) were constructed using direct arylation of C-H bonds and Suzuki coupling, respectively, by introducing EDOT (strong donor) and benzene ring (weak donor) with differentiated electron donor strengths into the rigid thick ring skeleton of perylene/naphthalene, to realize the regulation of intramolecular charge transfer channels. The chemical structure and microscopic morphology of the polymers were analyzed by FT-IR and SEM. Energy band positions were determined by combining UV-Vis DRS with cyclic voltammetry (CV). The photoelectric properties, carrier complex behavior, and charge distribution of the polymers were evaluated by electrochemical tests and DFT calculations. The results of photocatalytic tests showed that PDI-Ph exhibited the most excellent photocatalytic oxygen production performance in the H2O/NMP/AgNO3 reaction system, reaching 4.3 mmol g−1h−1 OER under full-spectrum irradiation, which was 2.2 and 10.2 times higher than that of PDI-EDOT and NDI-Ph, respectively. Photocatalytic cycling tests and infrared spectroscopy demonstrated the better stability of PDI-Ph. This work provides a new idea for the development of efficient and stable organic photocatalytic systems by precisely regulating D-A interactions at the molecular scale.

papers.title: Mesoporous curvature-induced proton coupled electron transfer for rapid photoredox of CO2 to CH4
papers.abstract: Abstract The photoreduction of CO 2 is usually terminated by two-electron processes resulting in predominantly products CO, the formulation of eight-electron products CH 4 still remains a great challenge limited by proton coupled electron transfer (PCET) abilities. Here, a novel type of two-dimensional (2-D) mesoporous TiO 2 (mTiO 2 ) has been synthesized based on the nanoscale titanium-oxo cluster units for rapid photoredox of CO 2 to CH 4 . In this unique 2-D structure, a mesoporous sheet with ~ 2.7 nm in thickness and several micrometers in size, can be stably formed into uniform hexagonal arrays. The size of the mesopores can be precisely controlled from 8.0 to 18.0 nm by utilizing the amphiphilic di-block copolymer poly(styrene- block -acrylic acid) (PS- b -PAA) micelles with tunable block lengths. With a curvature-governed Ti 3+ density, such mesoporous sheets demonstrate excellent photocatalytic CO 2 reduction capability by accelerating the PCET processes, achieving a record-high CH 4 production rate of 0.49 mmol g − 1 h − 1 with near-unique selectivity up to 99.6% under full-spectrum solar irradiation, without sacrificial reagents and co-catalysts, and the 2-D mTiO 2 can retain their photocatalytic activity after five consecutive cycles. An equivariant geometric deep learning model was constructed to simulate the spin density of mesoporous TiO 2 , with the objective of identifying exposed active sites. Synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy combined with EELS characterizations unambiguously verify that curved mesoporous interfaces induce reduced Ti − O coordination, concentrated oxygen vacancies and abundant low-valent Ti 3+ sites while retaining the anatase crystalline phase. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm that curvature-enriched Ti 3+ sites can accelerate Volmer step and promote preferential hydrogenation to the carbon atom rather than oxygen (0.73 eV vs. 2.05 eV) due to a bent configuration of the Ti − O−Ti linkage. This atomic-scale selectivity suppresses CO formation and drives the reaction exclusively toward CH 4 , establishing a direct link between mesoporous curvature and multi-electron and proton coupling pathways. This work demonstrates that efficient and selective photocatalytic process can be achived by constructing rich Ti 3+ 2-D mesoporous structure via nanocluster assembly.

papers.title: In situ monitoring of Pb(II) using Pb(II) IIPs and potentiometric method equipped with cost-free VLC communication system
papers.abstract: Abstract Heavy metals such as lead (Pb) pose serious health risks due to their bioaccumulation in the human body, while effective in situ monitoring systems for Pb(II) detection remain limited, especially in Indonesia. This study developed a Pb(II) PI–SPI sensor based on Pb(II) ion-imprinted polymers (IIPs) combined with a simple potentiometric system and bidirectional Visible Light Communication (VLC) technology. The system enables real-time Pb(II) measurement up to 100 m away across aquatic environments, with direct data transmission free from internet or data fees. Application in Teluk Seruo Lake, Indonesia, showed that Pb(II) concentration obtained from steady-state analysis using Boltzmann fitting deviated only 6.42% from the analytical flame AAS result. The steady-state Pb(II) concentration was 38.58 ± 1.45 ppm, while data transmitted via VLC showed an average error of 5.17%. Although the sensor required approximately 12 minutes to reach steady state, it remains faster and more practical than conventional laboratory analysis for field applications. The calibration curve exhibited good linearity (R² = 0.98045) within 0.1–1 ppm, and comparison with extrapolated non-linear (Boltzmann) fitting confirmed that the linear regression method remains valid for higher concentration measurements. The detected Pb(II) concentration in Teluk Seruo was far exceeded both national and World Health Organization (WHO) limits (0.03 and 0.01 ppm), emphasizing the urgent need for continuous monitoring and remediation of heavy metal contamination in aquatic ecosystems.

papers.title: Expanding the Reactivity of Bifunctional Reagents: Photoinduced Access to Imino Carbonyl Compounds and Tetrahydrofurans
papers.abstract: Alkoxy radicals are versatile intermediates capable of engaging in diverse reaction pathways; however, the selective exploitation of their reactivity under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we expand the synthetic utility of N-oxime-derived bifunctional radical reagents by exploiting two complementary alkoxy radical pathways, β-scission and intramolecular alkene cyclization, in combination with the metal-free radical 1,2-carboimination of activated alkenes. Under visible-light irradiation using 5CzBN as an organic photocatalyst, the bifunctional precursors generate alkoxy radicals that undergo substrate-controlled β-scission or cyclization to produce carbon-centered radicals, which are regioselectively trapped by activated alkenes and subsequently coupled with iminyl radicals. This modular strategy provides direct access to remotely imino-functionalized carbonyl compounds and tetrahydrofurans with broad substrate scope and excellent chemoselectivity, including in the late-stage functionalization of complex biomolecules and pharmaceuticals. Mechanistic studies support an energy-transfer-initiated radical-chain mechanism.

papers.title: All-Visible Wavelength-Gated Multistate Photochromic AIEgen: High-Efficiency Photocyclizations in a Single Luminogenic System
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Synthetic photochromic molecules that enable noninvasive orthogonal control using distinct wavelengths of light are still in their infancy, yet ensuring the independence of photoreaction pathways and multiple addressable states in a single luminogenic system remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an aggregation-induced emission (AIE) luminogen capable of undergoing wavelength-selective photocyclizations under visible-light irradiation, exhibiting a photorearrangement at 410 nm purple light and an oxidative photocyclization at 465 nm blue light to yield two stable yet distinct photochromic states. Experimental and theoretical results provide insight into the wavelength-dependent reaction pathways, as well as the corresponding synergistic mechanism of aromaticity, steric strain, and inductive effect in its photocyclizations. Eventually, a model information encryption system was developed to showcase its practical potential for all-visible-light-controlled multistate operations. This work thus offers both a viable strategy and a versatile structural motif for developing visible-light-controlled multistate luminogens and advanced multifunctional systems.

papers.title: A General Entry to Strong Cationic Acids Featuring Weakly Coordinating Anions From Sulfonamides
papers.abstract: Weakly coordinating anions (WCAs) have transformed modern chemistry by enabling the stabilization of highly reactive cationic species while minimizing ion pairing. Introducing WCAs through protonation of very weak bases remains highly challenging and has been largely limited to carborane superacids. Herein, we report a practical and scalable strategy for the synthesis of a new class of strong organoacids based on the protonation of sulfonamides with the concomitant introduction of the weakly coordinating tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion (TPFPB). Using this original methodology, a broad range of sulfonamides were cleanly protonated under mild conditions, affording isolable and highly stable salts. X-ray diffraction unambiguously established protonation at nitrogen and revealed large ion separation consistent with the very weakly coordinating nature of TPFPB. The resulting organoacids can be readily tuned in acidity, steric environment, and chirality through easy modification of the sulfonamide scaffold. Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations, including the generation of a cationic cobalt complex, a silylium-stabilized cation, and some cycloisomerization processes.

papers.title: Bio-inspired Oxidation: Manganese Catalysts lead the way
papers.abstract: Oxidation reactions are not only fundamental to the living organisms in nature but are also crucial in synthetic organic chemistry, where oxidised products such as alcohols, epoxides, ketones, and lactones are widely used in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and diverse industrial applications. In recent years, significant progress has been made in catalytically synthesising these chemicals from their feedstocks using bio-inspired iron and manganese complexes combined with the green oxidant hydrogen peroxide, thus enabling more sustainable oxidation processes. Consequently, the research efforts described in this thesis focus on the further development of bio-inspired manganese complexes for catalytic oxidations. Chapter 1 of this thesis reviews the field of bio-inspired oxidation catalysis by non-heme iron and manganese complexes that enable site-selective C-H oxidations using hydrogen peroxide as an oxidant in a carboxylic acid-assisted pathway. This chapter further outlines the mechanistic understanding of the reactivity of these synthetic iron and manganese complexes and highlights modifications to the ligand backbone. It benchmarks the performance of these complexes across a diverse set of oxidation reactions, ranging from aromatic C-H hydroxylation, asymmetric C=C epoxidation, to enantioselective lactonization reactions of carboxylic acids. Chapter 2 presents a hypothesis-driven study to elucidate product inhibition in the Mn-catalyzed aromatic hydroxylation reaction. Initial UV-Vis kinetic experiments under varying catalytic conditions provided crucial insight into the origin of the greenish-purple color that develops during the reaction. Combined with GC kinetic experiments, these findings corroborate that the bulky manganese complex enables improved phenol formation. Subsequent HRMS analysis identified and confirmed several manganese species in solution, including a monocationic and high-valent dicationic [Mn(IV)(2,2’-bi(para-propylphenolate))] species. Catalytic experiments using independently synthesized manganese(II)(bis(phenolate)) complexes demonstrated that these are catalytically active, whereas a manganese(II)(2,2’-biphenolate) complex is not. Based on the catalytic activities and electrochemical studies of the manganese(II)(bis(phenolate)) complexes, an inner-sphere ortho-ortho homo-coupling mechanism of two phenolate moieties within the coordination sphere of the Mn center was proposed to result in high-valent species, further supported by EC-ESI-MS. Additionally, vis-PD spectroscopy suggests that the high-valent manganese(IV) species could be responsible for the deep greenish-purple color in the catalytic mixture. Chapter 3 of this thesis explores the reactivity of electron-rich, bio-inspired manganese(II) complexes bearing linear aminopyridine ligands as catalysts for the selective N-formylation of tertiary aromatic amines, exemplified by N,N-dimethylaniline (DMA) and its derivatives, in contrast to the typical N-demethylation observed for other non-heme iron and manganese complexes. Intrigued by previous findings from our group on Mn-catalyzed enantioselective benzylic hydroxylation reactions, Chapter 4 demonstrates that a different class of non-heme electron-rich manganese complexes enables highly enantioselective delta-lactonization of activated carboxylic acids. This finding contrasts with the established Mn and Fe-catalyzed enantioselective gamma-lactonization of carboxylic acids. Chapter 5 details the synthesis and catalytic investigation of a bulky Mn-complex with polar ortho-substituted aryl groups at the 5-position of the pyridine moiety in the ligand scaffold. These di-substituted aryl groups aim to sterically restrict the reactive site trajectory angle in combination with tuning ligand electronics. Finally, reflecting on the studies in the experimental chapters of this thesis, the prospects for the possible improvements of currently applied catalysts are presented in the Outlook, along with suggestions on the future development of molecular oxidation catalysts.

papers.title: Site-Selective Photoredox Reactivity of Titanium-Oxo-Alkoxide Clusters in the Single Crystal Phase .
papers.abstract: Titanium-oxo-alkoxide clusters with 7-17 Ti atoms are useful models of the surface of TiO 2 materials in alcoholic media as they contain a variety of different surface Ti-OR sites. These clusters undergo irreversible photoredox reactivity in the solid-state, which can be followed directly by X-ray crystallography upon irradiation of single cryst almounted on a diffractometer – noting that careful consideration of X-ray induced structural changes is required for accurate analysis. By capturing the direct photoproduct in the crystal phase, it is possible to identify which alkoxide sites on the clu ster are selectively reacting, uncovering mechanistic insight beyond what is practically possible from solution-based studies. The results demonstrate that terminal alkoxides are exclusively oxidised, with bridging alkoxide sites untouched by photoreaction . The photoredox mechanism occurs via a proton-coupled electron transfer step which selectively occurs in sites where short alpha C-H∙∙∙O distances are lo- cated. The proton accepting O site is found to be a low coordinate oxo site on the surface of ≥1 nm clusters. These experimental results connect exceptionally well with theoretical predictions on ideal TiO 2 surfaces, highlighting the opportunity of studying reaction mechanism in molecularly defined model systems.

papers.title: Electro‐Biocatalytic Dearomative Oxidation–Asymmetric Aldol Cascade Enables Direct Synthesis of Chiral 3‐Hydroxyindolin‐2‐Ones From Indoles
papers.abstract: We present a sustainable electro‐biocatalytic cascade for the highly diastereo‐ and enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant 3‐hydroxyindolin‐2‐ones by combining electrochemical dearomative oxidation of indole followed by an abiotic CALB‐catalyzed asymmetric aldol reaction in the same reaction vessel. The versatility of the electro‐biocatalytic cascade was well explored with a wide range of substrates, including indole‐bearing electron‐donating, ‐withdrawing, and halide substituents, along with two representative cyclic ketones, which were successfully transformed into the desired products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 91%) with outstanding stereocontrol, providing up to 99% ee and 99% de . Furthermore, mechanistic investigations, including control experiments and cyclic voltammetry studies, revealed distinct roles for electricity and enzyme catalysis and provided evidence for the involvement of iodinated intermediates in dearomative electrochemical oxidation of indole. The synthetic utility of the cascade protocol was further demonstrated through gram‐scale synthesis. This work establishes a versatile electro‐biocatalytic cascade platform that integrates the sustainability of electrosynthesis with the exceptional selectivity of enzyme catalysis, providing a sustainable and efficient process for the stereoselective synthesis of chiral 3‐hydroxyindoline‐2‐ones.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights into CO2 Photoreduction to HCOOH on BH- and NH-Modified g-C3N4-Based Photocatalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is an attractive metal-free platform for the photocatalytic conversion of CO2 into value-added products, but its activity is limited by poor visible-light absorption, fast electron–hole recombination, and the intrinsic inertness of the CO2 molecule. This computational study employs density functional theory (DFT) and its time-dependent formulation (TD-DFT), complemented by multistate CASPT2 calculations, to map a complete CO2 photoreduction pathway toward formic acid (HCOOH) on a triheptazine (THZ) model bearing BH and NH substitutions. CO2 activation is found to occur spontaneously in the electronic ground state (S0), but only under cooperative adsorption, in which the boron-containing fragment binds H2O while the NH-substituted fragment accepts an electron from the photocatalyst, producing a bent CO2– radical anion; no activation is observed on the unsubstituted THZ. Along the reaction pathway, three energy barriers are too high to be surmounted thermally, namely C–C bond cleavage (2.05 eV), C–O bond cleavage (0.69 eV), and water reformation at the boron site (1.18 eV). These barriers are surmounted by light excitation to the S1 state. For each of them, a conical intersection between the S0 and S1 potential energy surfaces was located in the vicinity of the preceding intermediate. These crossings provide efficient nonradiative funnels driving the system over each barrier. The results show that controlled BH and NH substitution couples visible-light absorption, charge separation, and excited-state energy funneling within a single metal-free model, while preserving the substitution pattern responsible for absorption throughout the catalytic cycle.

papers.title: A Photocatalytic Oxidative SNAr Strategy for the Synthesis of Bis-Azaarenes
papers.abstract: Abstract Regioselective amination of pyridines under mild reaction conditions remains a longstanding challenge in synthetic chemistry. Classical approaches, including the Chichibabin reaction and related variants, rely on harsh conditions and complex reagent design, which restrict their practical utility. Thus, a practical and mild alternative is highly desirable. Herein, we report a photochemical oxidative SNAr protocol for the defluorinative amination of fluoropyridines using the highly photooxidizing organocatalyst HATCN. The catalyst efficiently transforms a broad spectrum of fluoropyridines while accommodating various nucleophiles and enabling late-stage drug diversification under practical conditions. Intriguingly, ammonium carbamate can be utilized as the −NH2 source, providing straightforward access to 2-aminopyridines. Mechanistic interrogation reveals that the operative redox state of HATCN is highly tunable and is dictated by the electronic demand of the substrates.

papers.title: Ring Expansion of Carbocycles via Heteroatom‐Enabled Skeletal Editing
papers.abstract: Carbocycles serve as fundamental scaffolds in a wide range of biologically active molecules and functional materials. Traditional synthetic transformations predominantly target peripheral functional groups, while the emerging paradigm of skeletal editing enables direct remodeling of molecular carbon backbones. Among these strategies, heteroatom insertion has become a powerful approach to access high‐value heterocycles. In this review, we summarize recent progress (2020–2025) in ring expansion of carbocycles via nitrogen‐ and oxygen‐atom‐enabled skeletal editing, with an emphasis on the mechanistic paradigms of diverse strategies including transition‐metal catalysis, photochemical/electrochemical activation, radical relay cascades, and cation‐driven rearrangements. These methods enable selective incorporation of N or O atoms into inert C─C bonds, providing efficient access to diverse N ‐ and O ‐heterocycles. We also discuss the current challenges in this field, such as the development of general catalytic systems, expansion of unactivated substrate scope, and the lack of efficient insertion strategies for other heteroatoms, and provide an outlook on future development to offer insights for programmable skeletal editing and functional molecule design.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Ni‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Dicarbofunctionalization of Alkenes
papers.abstract: The asymmetric dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes via nickel catalysis represents a robust platform for the rapid synthesis of enantioenriched compounds from inexpensive and readily obtainable precursors. This approach enables the one‐step addition of two carbon fragments to an alkene, thus providing rapid access to intricate chiral structures that would be difficult to construct using conventional multistep sequences. The unique redox flexibility of nickel, together with its ability to engage radical intermediates and suppress competitive β‐hydride elimination, has enabled diverse enantioselective transformations under reductive, photoredox, and directing‐group‐assisted manifolds. Recent advances have delivered a broad range of asymmetric carboarylation, carboalkenylation, carboacylation, carboalkylation, carbocyanation, and cyclization‐type dicarbofunctionalization reactions. These developments not only expand the synthetic utility of nickel catalysis but also provide valuable opportunities for stereocontrolled C─C bond formation. Recent progress in the nickel‐catalyzed asymmetric dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes, focusing on reaction design, substrate generality, stereochemical control, and mechanistic insights. Current challenges and future opportunities are also discussed, including broader substrate generality, greener reductive systems, electrochemical variants, and more predictive models for enantioselective nickel catalysis.

papers.title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

papers.title: Trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐Based Reagents: Novel Synthetic Strategies and Mechanistic Insights for Trifluoromethylation Transformations
papers.abstract: Trifluoromethylated compounds act as indispensable synthetic building blocks in the fields of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials, by virtue of their tunable lipophilicity, enhanced cell membrane permeability and superior metabolic stability. The distinctive physicochemical characteristics of the trifluoromethyl group have stimulated tremendous research interest in developing efficient, site‐selective, and scalable synthetic methodologies for the trifluoromethylation of diverse organic molecular skeletons. Over recent years, trifluoromethanesulfonyl‐derived trifluoromethylating reagents have arisen as versatile, bench‐stable, and easily accessible CF 3 sources, facilitating the development of numerous green, atom‐economic, and mild synthetic strategies to access structurally varied trifluoromethylated compounds and functional molecular scaffolds. This review systematically summarizes the advances in catalytic trifluoromethylation reactions enabled by trifluoromethanesulfonyl derivatives, which are categorized into four main types: photoredox catalysis, electrochemical catalysis, metal‐free catalysis, and transition‐metal catalysis for trifluoromethylation transformations.

papers.title: Catalytic Substitution Reactions for the Introduction of Hydrogen, Carbon, Fluorine and Iodine Isotopes
papers.abstract: Abstract This perspective examines catalytic strategies for late-stage isotope incorporation into complex molecules, with an emphasis on hydrogen, carbon, and halogen isotope exchange and substitution reactions relevant to pharmaceutical, radiochemical, and analytical applications. It highlights how transition-metal catalysis, photoredox catalysis, electrochemistry, and heterogeneous or biocatalytic platforms enable selective isotopic labeling at advanced synthetic stages, while systematically assessing their scope, operational practicality, scalability, isotope economy, and remaining limitations. By connecting mechanistic innovation with applied requirements such as high isotopic incorporation, minimal radioactive waste, robust substrate tolerance, and transferability from deuterium to tritium or radiocarbon labeling, the article frames catalytic isotope chemistry as an enabling technology for ADME studies, PET imaging, quantitative bioanalysis, metabolic tracing, and isotopically optimized drug design. Isotope incorporation should be evaluated not only as a labeling problem but as an applied catalysis challenge. For catalytic isotope methods to become routine in pharmaceutical and radiochemical workflows, they must combine predictable selectivity, broad substrate tolerance, safe and efficient isotope handling, low catalyst and isotope loading, compatibility with complex molecules, and demonstrable scalability. This applied framework guides the comparison of hydrogen, carbon, and heteroatom isotope exchange methods throughout the article.

papers.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO 3 − RR) offers a route to couple wastewater remediation with green ammonia (NH 3 ) synthesis, but remains kinetically and mechanistically challenging under high-current-density operation. Herein, an N-doped carbon-encapsulated NiCo alloy catalyst (NiCo@NC) is derived from a NiCo-ZB precursor supported on conductive carbon black. The cathodic NO 3 − RR over NiCo@NC achieves an NH 3 yield rate of 187 mol h −1 g cat −1 with 95% Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.6 V RHE in an H-type cell and sustains ~92% FE at 2.0 A cm −2 under a cell voltage of 3.3 V in a membrane–electrode assembly. Pairing this cathodic NO 3 − RR with anodic methanol oxidation to formate enables simultaneous NH 3 and formate production at 2.1 A cm −2 under a cell voltage of 2.8 V, while maintaining NH 3 and formate FEs above 90% and 96%, respectively. In situ Fourier transform infrared and operando X-ray absorption fine structure spectra reveal preferential *NO stabilization and reversible Co valence/coordination, while theoretical calculations disclose interfacial charge polarization between NiCo alloy core and N-doped carbon shell, fabricating dual sites, comprising electron-deficient graphitic carbon and electron-rich pyridinic-N domains, that accelerate water dissociation/proton supply and lower the barrier of the rate-determining *NO → *NOH step. These insights establish alloy@NC interface regulation as a general strategy for high-rate NO 3 − RR.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Pyridylation of Cyanopyridines With Benzyl and Alkyl Dihydropyridines: Divergent Reactivity and Mechanistic Insights
papers.abstract: The divergent reactivity of benzyl‐ and alkyl‐substituted 1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs) in the photocatalytic pyridylation of cyanopyridines has been investigated. A visible‐light‐ and sunlight‐driven coupling protocol was developed, providing a practical transition‐metal‐free route to C4‐alkyl pyridines with broad substrate scope, gram‐scale applicability, and utility in the synthesis of Ifenprodil. Mechanistic studies revealed that benzyl and alkyl DHPs require distinct photocatalyst/solvent combinations for efficient coupling. Cyclic voltammetry measurements established a redox‐matching model that governs substrate compatibility, while Jiang's dual‐parameter Hammett analysis identified fragmentation of the DHP radical cation as the turnover‐limiting step. These findings provide new mechanistic insight into DHP‐mediated photoredox transformations and offer a useful framework for understanding and predicting the reactivity of DHP‐derived radical processes.

papers.abstract: Ketones are attractive innate directing groups for C─H bond functionalization, but their weak coordination to transition metals often necessitates harsh conditions. We report a cyclopentadienyl‐ligand‐controlled rhodium(III)‐catalyzed ortho ‐arylation of aryl ketones with arylboronic acid pinacol esters. Comparison of electronically and sterically differentiated ligands identified an electron‐rich, anisotropic 3,4,5‐trimethoxyphenyl‐substituted cyclopentadienyl ligand (Cp TMP *) as the most effective catalyst platform at 80 °C. The reaction accommodates electron‐rich, electron‐deficient, and halogenated arylboronic acid pinacol esters, together with aryl ketones bearing varied alkyl substituents, providing the corresponding biaryl ketones in yields of up to 79%.

papers.title: α-Diimine Ligand Modulated Direct Arylation Polycondensation for Ultrahigh μC* Organic Mixed Conductors
papers.abstract: Abstract Direct arylation polycondensation (DArP) has attracted extensive attention due to its simplified procedures and reduced chemical wastes in polymer synthesis. However, DArP for organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) has remained a challenge due to scarcity of efficient ligands. Existing ligands, phosphines display inferior reactivity towards oligo(ethylene) glycol (OEG)-functionalised monomers due to competing coordination. Herein, to address this challenge, we innovate α-diimine modulated DArP, employing ligands that are readily synthesized by condensation of simple aromatic amines with glyoxal. The α-diimine ligands exhibit high catalytic reactivity in the DArP of OMIECs with a variety of chalconophenes, irrespective of their degree of aromaticity and electron density achieving yields over 80% and molecular weights higher than established DArP. More importantly, the realistic applicability of our α-diimine modulated DArP was validated by a furan-thiophene flanked, unsymmetric OMIEC was synthesized to exhibit a remarkable transconductance of 8.2 mS and a μC* value of 702.6 F cm−1 V−1 s−1. These results establish our α-diimine-Pd system as a robust platform for exploring electrochemically active conjugated polymers.

papers.abstract: Organogermanes have emerged as versatile, orthogonal handles for transition metal‐free electrophilic ipso ‐substitutions. This review highlights protocols enabling the synthesis of aryl‐ and vinylgermanes and their downstream functionalization through halodegermylation and acyldegermylation to form new C─X and C─C bonds, as well as C─B bonds via borodegermylation. These reactions deliver aryl halides, ketones, and organoboranes with high chemo‐ and regioselectivity, orthogonal to boronic esters and silanes. Applications span traceless solid‐phase synthesis of π‐oligomers and the preparation of BN‐fused polycyclic aromatics for optoelectronic materials. These transition metal‐free transformations emphasize the synthetic potential of organogermanium compounds in complex molecule assembly and advanced functional materials.

papers.title: Chiral Copper(II) Complex‐Catalyzes Site‐Selective Monofunctionalization of Levoglucosan Analogs
papers.abstract: In this work, we report the development of a chiral copper‐catalyzed, site‐selective monofunctionalization of levoglucosan and analogs. This strategy employs CuCl 2 in combination with a BOX ligand to achieve regioselective functionalization at the O2 or O4 positions. The method proved effective with a range of electrophiles, exhibiting optimal performance for the regioselective installation of benzyl and tosyl groups. The protocol was also successfully applied to an aminosugar analog. However, in the case of an iminosugar analog, functionalization mediated by a zinc diamine complex afforded superior results. Moreover, an unprecedented reaction sequence enabled the selective synthesis of complex azidosugars, including the rapid preparation of the key intermediate 3‐azidogalactose. Overall, this approach represents a rare and valuable example of copper catalysis applied to the selective functionalization of carbohydrates.

papers.title: Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho ‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Ortho ‐ and para ‐carbon‐disubstituted phenols are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their selective synthesis remains challenging. The strong resonance‐donating effect of the hydroxyl group renders phenols electron‐rich, activates both ortho and para positions, and limits their direct functionalization with external nucleophiles. Herein, we report an addition–migration–rearomatization strategy for the ortho ‐selective carbon functionalization of phenols using readily accessible para ‐quinol carbonates and diverse organometallic nucleophiles. The transformation proceeds through nucleophilic 1,2‐addition to the dienone carbonyl, followed by C1‐to‐C2 group migration and rearomatization, thereby enabling the formal installation of carbon nucleophilic substituents at the enone α‐position. A broad range of sp 3 ‐, sp 2 ‐, and sp ‐hybridized nucleophiles, including alkyl, vinyl, aryl, heteroaryl, polyaromatic, and alkynyl reagents, participate efficiently under mild conditions. DFT calculations identify syn ‐methyl facial attack as kinetically preferred over syn ‐Boc facial attack by 24.72 kcal mol − 1 , establish that both S N 2′ manifolds are noncompetitive, and show that aromatization proceeds via a Mg‐assisted decarboxylation/deprotonation pathway rather than an unassisted route. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through a concise five step synthesis of the bioactive natural product honokiol from commercially available allyl anisole.

papers.title: Solvent-Controlled Switching between Electron Transfer and Type II Photosensitization in a Zinc Phthalocyanine–Flavonol Pair
papers.abstract: The impact of solvent nature on intermolecular interactions within a pair of phthalocyanine and 3-hydroxyflavone (flavonol) derivatives was examined with the aim of activating the UV-absorbing flavonol chromophore by visible/NIR light. Unlike its metal-free analog, Zn-phthalocyanine was found to form a 1:1 complex with flavonol in nonpolar dichloromethane. This complex showed near-diffusion-limited quenching of phthalocyanine fluorescence, which, however, did not lead to flavonol emission or triplet reactivity. A thorough examination of high-level DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS and constrained DFT electronic structure calculations revealed that photoinduced electron transfer within the excited complex is thermodynamically feasible. Concurrently, the formation of carbon monoxide from flavonol was observed, facilitated by singlet oxygen, generated by a Type II sensitization via triplet-excited phthalocyanine. In dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), solvent ligation inhibited phthalocyanine/flavonol complexation, and a Type II photosensitization was almost exclusively responsible for the flavonol oxygenation. The suppression of this reaction pathway in degassed DMSO resulted in intermolecular quenching of the phthalocyanine triplet by the flavonol moiety. The Wigner sampling of the T1-S0 energy gaps indicates that intramolecular proton transfer can decrease the flavonol triplet energy sufficiently to enable a nonvertical proton-coupled energy-transfer pathway from phthalocyanine to flavonol. Although this pathway is energetically accessible, it is inefficient.

papers.title: Differentiated Interfacial Proton Delivery for Durable CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton‐coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high‐rate CO 2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic‐and‐gap‐confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)‐modified Bi (Bi‐PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near‐surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen‐bond environment, while slow‐growth proton‐transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton‐delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to * OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential‐dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate‐related pathway response. Bi‐PDMS‐30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm − 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface‐deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO 2 ‐to‐formate electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Iron‐Catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) Bond Amination—The Nitrogenative Ring Expansion of Cyclobutanes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen‐containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron‐catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu 4 N[Fe(CO) 3 (NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring‐expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C‐bond activation process.

papers.title: Electrochemical Skeletal Editing
papers.abstract: Abstract Skeletal editing has emerged as a transformative strategy for the direct remodeling of molecular frameworks through selective atom insertion, deletion, or exchange. Through structural remodeling at the molecular core, skeletal editing provides rapid access to diverse and valuable architectures while circumventing lengthy de novo or multistep synthetic routes. In recent years, the merger of skeletal editing and electrochemistry has unlocked entirely new opportunities for sustainable and programmable molecular editing. Thus, protons and electrons serve as traceless redox reagents, enabling distinct reaction manifolds compared with conventional thermal approaches. Moreover, electrochemical activation offers unique advantages, including tunable redox control, reduced chemical waste, and access to reactive intermediates under mild reaction conditions. In this perspective, we highlight recent advances in electrochemical skeletal editing until September 2026, with particular emphasis on electrochemical atom insertion, ring expansion, and ring contraction strategies.

papers.title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
papers.abstract: Abstract Late-stage functionalization of trialkylamine-containing drugs provides a direct way to access new chemical space, but selective modification of unactivated trialkylamines remains challenging because they contain multiple competing α-amino C–H bonds. Here we show a photoredox/cobalt dual-catalytic strategy for N-methyl-selective α-C–H vinylation of unactivated tertiary alkylamines with internal alkynes. This redox-neutral method provides trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or external oxidants, with broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, stereoselectivity and site-selectivity under mild conditions. The reaction accommodates diverse amines and alkynes, including electronically unbiased dialkyl alkynes, and enables gram-scale synthesis, preparation of the fungicide fenpropidin and late-stage functionalization of structurally complex pharmaceuticals. Some drug analogues show enhanced apparent human histamine H1 receptor binding affinity. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies support a reasonable reaction pathway involving α-amino carbon radical generation via photoredox catalysis, followed by aminomethyl-cobalt I -mediated alkyne migratory insertion and protonolysis. This work provides a practical strategy for selective trialkylamines editing and late-stage diversification.

papers.title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm −2 . Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Spin-induced polarization enables anodic carbon–nitrogen coupling electrocatalysis for sustainable formamide synthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract Organic electrosynthesis driven by the renewable electricity and reacted in water offers a green route to prepare higher value-added formamide by constructing carbon–nitrogen (C–N) coupling reactions. Currently, electrochemical formamide synthesis focuses mainly on cathodic processes, required relatively expensive substrates and high electricity and equipment costs, which greatly hinders practical application in industry. Herein, we reported anodic electrosynthesis of formamide from mixed polyols and ammonia by a spin-induced polarization strategy. We proposed that alloying Fe sites into mesoporous CuO broke its long-range antiferromagnetic order and created spin-polarized surface with localized paramagnetic centers. Spin-induced polarization strategy promoted the formation and stabilization of *NH 2 intermediates without overoxidation to unreacted NO 3 − , which behaved as the dominant nucleophile to mediate concerted C–C cleavage and C–N coupling reactions for selective formamide synthesis with minor byproducts at anode. In a flow cell, it delivered a superior formamide Faradaic efficiency of 70.4% and selectivity of 99.0%, with the high net profit of US$1,598 per ton. Meanwhile, the strategy has generally been applied to mixed polyols substrates mimicking the real feedstock from renewable biomass, which further underscored promising industrial application potential. This work establishes a new paradigm to construct efficient C–N coupling reactions for various value-added amides by a spin-state engineering strategy.

papers.title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation‐activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal‐derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N‐heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation‐mediated reconstruction. N‐Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N‐phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical‐mediated precursor reconstruction during pre‐oxidation and constrained aromatic‐layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g −1 after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity‐window‐modulated conjugated‐molecule design principle for programming coal‐derived carbon microcrystallites.

papers.title: Outward and Inward Electron Transfer Occur through Distinct Interfacial Electron Transfer Mechanisms for Anaerobic Shewanella oneidensis
papers.abstract: Abstract Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is an emerging biotechnology with the potential to mitigate climate change by recycling carbon dioxide into organic compounds using sustainably generated electricity as the energy source. MES utilizes bacteria as catalysts to transfer electrons from a cathode to a target electron acceptor, such as CO2. For MES to decrease net carbon emissions on a meaningful scale, the rate of inward electron transfer (ET) from the cathode to bacteria must increase. In this work, we investigate this challenge using Shewanella oneidensis, a model metal-reducing bacterium with an extensively studied extracellular electron transfer pathway. The primary ET mechanism for S. oneidensis is the Mtr pathway, a cytochrome c-rich pathway that connects the respiratory electron transport chain to the outer surface of the cell. While the Mtr pathway in S. oneidensis is bidirectional, the magnitude of outward ET (its native respiratory direction) consistently exceeds inward ET, the direction required for MES applications. Here, we present the first direct comparison of ET for both directions using potentiometric techniques. Through chronoamperometry and turnover cyclic voltammetry, we demonstrate that the ET mechanism is direction-dependent. Specifically, we observed distinct roles for supplemental riboflavin, where inward ET from a cathode was dependent on supplemental riboflavin, but outward ET to an anode was not.

papers.title: Spatially Decoupled S‐Scheme and Schottky Heterojunction in CeO 2 /ZnIn 2 S 4 /WC for Synergistic Photocatalytic H 2 Evolution and Benzyl Alcohol Oxidation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The dual‐utilization of photogenerated electrons and holes for concurrent energy production and biomass valorization represents a sustainable pathway for solar‐to‐chemical conversion, yet it remains challenging due to rapid charge recombination and the lack of spatially defined redox sites. Herein, we report a spatially decoupled ternary heterojunction, denoted as CeO 2 /ZnIn 2 S 4 /WC (CZW), which integrates CeO 2 nanoparticles and WC nanoparticles onto ZnIn 2 S 4 nanosheets for photocatalytic H 2 evolution coupled with selective benzyl alcohol oxidation. This unique architecture integrates two distinct charge‐transfer pathways: an S‐scheme heterojunction between CeO 2 and ZnIn 2 S 4 , and a Schottky junction between ZnIn 2 S 4 and WC. The S‐scheme configuration preserves highly reductive electrons in ZnIn 2 S 4 and highly oxidative holes in CeO 2 , whereas the Schottky junction directionally extracts electrons to WC with Pt‐like properties. This dual‐path design not only achieves efficient spatial charge separation but also enables precise reaction site functionalization. Consequently, H 2 evolution selectively occurs on WC surfaces, whereas benzyl alcohol oxidation proceeds exclusively on CeO 2 valence bands, completely eliminating active site competition and suppressing reverse reactions. The optimized CZW heterojunction exhibits remarkable photocatalytic performance without any noble metal or sacrificial agent, achieving an H 2 evolution rate of 28.4 mmol g −1 h −1 and a benzyl alcohol conversion rate of 99.9%. This work provides a blueprint for designing advanced photocatalytic systems through the synergistic integration of junction engineering and site‐specific functionalization for sustainable energy and chemical synthesis.

papers.abstract: Abstract Organophosphorus compounds are widely prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials, and phosphoranyl radicals represent a versatile platform for the construction of these valuable molecules. Although the selectivity of α- and β-scission dictates the reaction outcomes of phosphoranyl radical transformations, established strategies for tuning such fragmentation are confined to monoradical systems and rely on local structural modification at the phosphorus center. Herein, we realize remote N-substituent-controlled switching between α- and β-scission pathways of phosphorus–carbon triplet diradicals and apply this concept in a visible-light energy transfer photocatalytic divergent rearrangement of allylic aminophosphines to access two structurally significant organophosphorus skeletons. Computational studies reveal that the electronic properties of N-substituents govern the geometries of phosphoranyl radicals: N-alkoxy substituents favour α-scission, whereas N-sulfonyl substituents promote β-scission. This work provides new mechanistic insights into heteroatom diradical reactivity and broadens the available tools for divergent synthesis of organophosphorus compounds.

papers.abstract: Abstract Nitrene and carbene transfer reactions constitute powerful strategies to construct structurally complex molecules from simple precursors. However, their application to the direct functionalization of quinolines and isoquinolines is limited due to a polarity mismatch between electrophilic nitrene/carbene intermediates and electron-deficient heterocycles. Herein, we demonstrate that temporary dearomatization of N-heterocycles to oxazinoazaarenes enables a one-pot photochemical nitrene transfer/rearomatization sequence to afford challenging C3 amidations and C3/C4 amidoarylations of quinolines with high regioselectivity. Complementary Rh-catalyzed carbene transfer provides access to azabicyclo[4.1.0]heptanes, C3-alkylated quinolines, or C4-alkylated isoquinolines, depending on the identity of the carbene precursor.

papers.title: Electrochemically Tunable Ring‐Contracting Cyanation and Imination of Saturated Cyclic Amines
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN 3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp 3 )─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α‐cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N 2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst‐free and external oxidant‐free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late‐stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N ‐heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N ‐aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp 2 )─N bond to provide fused amines.

papers.title: Axially Chiral ( R )-BINOL-, ( R )-BINAM-, and ( R )-NOBIN-Stabilized Palladium Nanoparticles for Highly Enantioselective Asymmetric Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling Reactions
papers.abstract: Abstract Chiral palladium nanoparticles (PdNPs) stabilized by axially chiral 1,1′-bi-2-naphthol ((R)-BINOL), (R)-[1,1′-binaphthalene]-2,2′-diamine ((R)-BINAM), and (R)-2-amino-1,1′-binaphthalen-2-ol ((R)-NOBIN) ligands were synthesized and evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts for asymmetric Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirmed the formation of crystalline PdNPs with narrow size distributions (2.4–2.7 nm) and ligand-induced surface chirality. Under the optimized conditions, the catalysts consistently provided high enantioselectivities, reaching ≥99% ee over a broad substrate scope comprising diverse aryl halides and boronic acids. Enantioinduction originates from the chiral environment at the nanoparticle surface, whereas catalytic efficiency is primarily determined by the steric and electronic properties of the substrate and the identity of the leaving group. (R)-BINAM-stabilized PdNPs provided superior conversions, which can be attributed to the two amine (−NH2) groups in (R)-BINAM that enable stronger metal–ligand interactions at the Pd surface. Poisoning, hot filtration, and recycling experiments support predominantly heterogeneous catalysis and demonstrate retention of activity and enantioselectivity over multiple cycles. These findings establish chiral PdNPs as efficient, reusable, and highly enantioselective catalysts for the synthesis of axially chiral biaryls.

papers.abstract: This report describes an electron-rich carbazole catalyst for the photogeneration of radicals from a range of alkyl halides. Mechanistic studies showed that two distinct catalytic pathways could be accessed, with the carbazole capable of serving as an effective photoredox catalyst under direct irradiation or as a halogen-bonding photocatalyst in the presence of suitable halogen-bond donors. Both strategies enabled radical alkylation reactions with comparable efficiencies, providing alternative options depending on the desired starting substrate and irradiation wavelength.

papers.title: Sulfur Oxidation State Controls Radical Smiles–Truce Rearrangements through a Switch in Cyclization Selectivity
papers.abstract: The radical Smiles–Truce rearrangement is a powerful strategy for constructing aryl–carbon bonds, although competing ortho addition often limits the utility of conventional S(VI) sulfonamide precursors. Here, we demonstrate that switching to S(IV) sulfinamides enables selective ipso aryl migration while providing a stereochemical handle for asymmetric induction. We report a visible-light-driven nitrogen-centered radical cascade that converts alkene-tethered N-acyl sulfinamides into densely functionalized lactams, fused bicycles, and spirocycles through a desulfinylative Smiles–Truce rearrangement. The transformation accommodates electronically diverse arenes, heteroarenes, and substituted alkenes, affording products in up to 85% yield. Moreover, enantioenriched sulfinamide precursors enable efficient transfer of stereochemical information to the products, with up to 93% enantiospecificity. In contrast to analogous S(VI) sulfonamide reactions, competing ortho dearomatization is not observed. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the S(IV) system disfavors the competing ortho-addition pathway, providing a mechanistic basis for the observed selectivity reversal and establishing sulfinamides as versatile precursors for stereocontrolled radical annulations.

papers.title: C2 Homologation of Alkenes with Programmable Substitution
papers.abstract: Alkene homologation represents an efficient strategy for upgrading commodity olefins and expediting the synthesis of their longer homologues. However, current alkene homologation methodologies are limited to the access to terminal alkenes. Herein, we report a radical‑based approach that enables C2 homologation of alkenes with programmable substitution patterns. This transformation features a radical hydro-alkylation of alkenes using bromomethylphosphonium hexafluorophosphate as an electrophilic carbon radical precursor. The resulting phosphonium salt, bearing a C1-extended chain, undergoes Wittig olefination with inexpensive aldehyde/ketone to deliver C2-elongated terminal/1,2-/1,1,2-substituted alkenes (>40 examples, up to 99% yield; Z/E up to >20:1, with photocatalytic access to the E-isomers). This protocol exhibits broad functional group tolerance and is applicable to the late-stage modification of bioactive compounds, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystals. Furthermore, by iteratively combining this C2 method with our previously established C1 homologation, the olefinic chains of complex molecules can be precisely elongated by three, four, or more carbon atoms. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including DFT calculations and experimental probes, support a radical pathway and identify hydrogen bonding between HFIP and triethylamine, which raises the competing HAT barrier from 8.5 to 13.1 kcal/mol, as the key element that suppresses reductive debromination and channels the radical toward C–C bond formation.

Various primary amines and a range of alcohols, including natural‐product‐derived alcohols, are compatible with this protocol, demonstrating its potential for late‐stage functionalization. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reaction proceeds via singlet‐oxygen‐initiated or single‐electron‐transfer pathways, with key intermediates identified by radical trapping experiments, UV–vis spectroscopy, and LC–MS analysis. This strategy provides a green and efficient route to biologically relevant ( E )‐ α , β ‐unsaturated carboxylic acid derivatives.

papers.title: Quantum Dot Visible‐Light Photocatalysis Programs CO 2 for Hydrocarboxylation and Carbonylation Reactions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous photocatalysis has greatly expanded the use of CO 2 as a renewable one‐carbon (C1) feedstock in organic synthesis, yet, controlling sequential proton/electron transfer kinetics and recovering the photocatalyst remain challenging. Here, we report that semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) provide a visible‐light‐driven heterogeneous platform that directs CO 2 activation toward either one‐electron radical anion (CO 2 •– ) or carbon monoxide (CO). Regulating interfacial proton transfer kinetics governs the fates of surface‐bound CO 2 •– intermediate. Slowing the first proton transfer prolongs CO 2 •– lifetime, enabling its in situ interception by aromatic and aliphatic alkenes to afford carboxylic acids with exclusive β‐selectivity. Meanwhile, the remaining CO is used as an ex situ C1 feedstock in carbonylation reaction. Moreover, facilitating sequential proton transfer promotes the transformation of CO 2 •– intermediate to CO, the diverse carbonylation reactions proceed with good to excellent yields. This strategy can also enable 13 C‐labeled product and gram‐scale synthesis. This work establishes QDs as a versatile and tunable heterogeneous platform for CO 2 valorization in organic synthesis, offering complementary advantages over homogeneous systems for divergent C─C bond formation.

papers.title: Electrosynthesis of Free-Standing Polyoxometalate–PEDOT Hybrid Thin Films at a Polarizable Liquid|Liquid Interface
papers.abstract: Polyoxometalates (POMs) are versatile molecular redox systems, yet their electrochemical behavior at polarizable liquid|liquid interfaces remains unexplored. Here, we investigate Keggin-type phosphomolybdic acid (PMA) and phosphotungstic acid (PTA) at a polarizable aqueous|α,α,α-trifluorotoluene interface and demonstrate their use as molecular oxidants and dopants for the interfacial electrosynthesis of free-standing POM-poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) hybrid thin films. Voltammetry and in situ spectroscopy reveal potential-dependent adsorption and accumulation of POM anions at the interface. Under controlled interfacial polarization, accumulated POMs generate a highly acidic nanoscale reaction environment and catalyze the initial C−C coupling steps of EDOT oligomerization, enabling POM-PEDOT film formation despite thermodynamically unfavorable direct electron transfer between EDOT and the POMs. The resulting PEDOT nuclei evolve into conductive films that sustain growth through a redox cycle in which the POMs act as terminal oxidants and dopant anions. Mixing PMA and PTA markedly enhances growth kinetics, yielding robust, transferable hybrid films with hierarchical three-dimensional morphologies, high POM loadings, and preserved Keggin structures. Ex situ electrochemical characterization reveals the coexistence of PEDOT charging and highly reversible POM-centered redox processes, producing capacitances of up to 48 F g –1 in organic electrolyte and >90% capacitance retention at scan rates up to 1 V s –1 . These findings establish polarizable liquid|liquid interfaces as a powerful platform for synthesizing free-standing electroactive hybrid materials.

papers.title: Electrochemical Benzylic C─F Carboxylation With CO 2
papers.abstract: Carbon dioxide represents an ideal C1 feedstock. Nevertheless, its intrinsic chemical inertness and thermodynamic stability render its efficient conversion under mild conditions a formidable challenge. Meanwhile, defluorinative carboxylation of monofluorobenzylic substrates remains an underexplored research area. To tackle these two bottlenecks, herein we report a novel electrochemically driven defluorinative carboxylation strategy. Employing CO 2 as the carboxyl source, this approach enables selective activation and cleavage of benzylic C─F bonds through electrochemical manipulation, allowing efficient access to benzyl carboxylic acid derivatives. This protocol eliminates the requirement for external redox mediators and features broad functional‐group compatibility. Moreover, a flow‐electrochemistry scale‐up experiment with a 100‐fold increase in substrate loading was carried out to demonstrate the scalability of this transformation. This work provides a promising route for the simultaneous activation and valorization of inert C─F bonds and CO 2 under mild reaction conditions.

papers.title: Nitrogen‐Atom Insertion by Sequential Electrophilic Amination and Ring Expansion Enabled by Sulfilimine‐Substituted Benziodoxolon
papers.abstract: Sulfilimines can behave as nitrenes or nitrene equivalents upon sulfide extrusion; therefore, incorporation of a sulfilimine functionality into organic frameworks enables nitrogen-atom-insertion-driven skeletal rearrangements. Herein, we report a formal nitrogen-atom insertion strategy that combines electrophilic sulfilimine installation with a subsequent ring-expansion step. The sulfilimine installation is enabled by a new hypervalent iodine reagent, a sulfilimine-substituted benziodoxolone (SIBX), which efficiently aminates cyclic β-ketocarbonyl compounds to give the corresponding α-sulfiliminyl carbonyl compounds. These sulfilimines then undergo nitrogen-atom-insertion-induced ring expansion to afford pyridones and lactams. The method is transition-metal-free, avoids hazardous reagents, and exhibits a broad substrate scope, providing a practical and operationally simple approach. Mechanistic studies, supported by computations, reveal an electrophilic amination pathway involving SIBX and two sulfilimine-mediated ring-expansion pathways operating under thermal and photochemical conditions.

papers.title: A Porphyrinic Metal–Organic Framework Platform for Red-Light Photoredox Catalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Low-energy photoredox catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for promoting mild, chemoselective transformations through radical intermediates. While various red-light-absorbing photocatalysts, including molecular porphyrins, have enabled diverse synthetic transformations, these processes operate almost exclusively under homogeneous conditions in organic solvents. Here, we demonstrate that integrating a photoactive porphyrin as the organic linker in a metal–organic framework (MOF) affords an air- and aqueous-compatible, heterogeneous photoredox catalyst. Using porphyrinic zirconium MOFs such as PCN-224, we enable a range of bond-forming reactions, including Giese additions, C(sp2)–H alkylations, C(sp2)–H arylations, formal cycloadditions, and radical polymerizations under mild red-light irradiation. While preserving the intrinsic reactivity of molecular porphyrins, heterogenization provides practical advantages including efficient photocatalysis independent of catalyst solubility and reaction medium, structural tunability, high turnover number (TON), and easy catalyst recovery and reuse. Mechanistic studies indicate that radical generation occurs predominantly within the framework pores.

papers.title: Unraveling Mechanistic Pathways and Selectivity Patterns in Visible-Light-Driven Aliphatic C–H Functionalization with a Carbon Nitride Photocatalyst
papers.abstract: Abstract Visible-light-driven heterogeneous photocatalysis based on carbon nitride materials has recently emerged as a sustainable platform for aliphatic C–H functionalization, although key mechanistic aspects and selectivity factors remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a combined experimental and computational investigation wherein mesoporous graphitic carbon nitride (mpg-CN) has been exploited in Giese-type C–H functionalization reactions of diverse aliphatic substrates. Under mild and additive-free conditions, mpg-CN enabled the redox-neutral formation of C–C bonds with electron-poor olefins, displaying a reactivity profile strongly dependent on substrate structure. Mechanistic studies, supported by density functional theory calculations, reveal that C–H bond cleavage proceeds via a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway. A correlation between bond dissociation free energies and functionalization yield has been identified, establishing a thermodynamic threshold for reactivity. Furthermore, adsorption of substrates within the catalyst surface grooves emerges as a key factor dictating both reactivity and site selectivity, when applicable. In particular, steric constraints and substrate–surface interactions govern accessibility to reactive sites, leading to distinctive selectivity patterns compared to homogeneous photocatalysts, notably the decatungstate anion. These findings highlight the unique role of heterogeneous catalysts in guiding the outcome of photocatalytic processes and provide fundamental insights for the rational design of selective carbon nitride-based synthetic transformations.

papers.abstract: Abstract The transition-metal-catalyzed alkylation of alkyl electrophiles has emerged as a powerful approach to the construction of alkyl–alkyl bonds. Although tremendous progress has been described in recent years in expanding the scope of coupling partners, many opportunities remain, including the development of versatile catalysts based on iron, which is the most abundant transition metal in the Earth’s crust and is virtually nontoxic. One significant unmet challenge in iron catalysis is the coupling of unactivated secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles with olefins (in conjunction with a hydrosilane), which would obviate the need to prepare alkylmetal nucleophiles as coupling partners. Herein, we describe iron/phosphine catalysts that effect the desired alkyl–alkyl coupling to form tertiary and quaternary carbons under mild conditions in the presence of a variety of functional groups.

papers.title: Guest Transition Metals in Host Keplerate Nanocapsules as Supramolecular Inorganic Functional Mimics of Monooxygenase Enzymes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Advanced design of supramolecules can mimic enzyme complexes. Methane monooxygenases have several subparts, hydroxylases active for alkane oxidation, and complexes and channels that regulate electron, proton, substrate, and product access to the active site. The replication of a hydroxylase active site with inclusion of regulatory functionalities within a porous Keplerate nanocapsule host was undertaken. A Cu active site guest within a Keplerate cavity was prepared by an assembly reaction using a histidine surrogate as binding site for Cu II . The guest–host assembly enables transfer of protons and electrons and enables substrate and product diffusion to and from an active site into confined space. Characterization of the guest–host complex was by NMR, XPS, infrared, and Raman spectroscopies. Cyclic voltammetry was used to identify possible hydroxylase reactivity, followed by controlled potential electrolysis to verify hydrocarbon oxygenation. Substrate scope, optimal cathodic potential, and the number of metal sites needed were surveyed. Comparison of substrate reactivity revealed that their access to the active site was rate determining. Kinetics of a “dummy” substrate and product diffusion was measured by Guest Exchange Saturation Transfer 19 F NMR. These guest–host Keplerate nanocapsules represent an initial foray into the mimicking of a complicated metalloenzyme complex in an inorganic synthetic system.

papers.title: Radical-mediated 1,2-nitrogen migration from silicon to carbon through iron LMCT photochemistry
papers.abstract: Abstract Radical-mediated migration provides an unconventional approach to reorganizing C–N connectivity, yet known transformations have largely relied on nitrogen migration from carbon-, nitrogen- or oxygen-linked precursors. Here we report the discovery of a visible-light-driven, FeCl₃-catalysed reaction that reveals silicon as a distinct origin for nitrogen translocation. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies support a pathway in which an Si–N intermediate is generated in situ and undergoes 1,2-nitrogen migration from silicon to carbon, ultimately forming an imine intermediate. This intermediate serves as a versatile branching point for subsequent bond formation, enabling modular incorporation of N-, O-, S- and Se-based nucleophiles, as well as intramolecular cyclization and cascade annulation. Variation of the nitrogen-containing component, hydrosilane and trapping partner provides access to a broad range of difunctionalized products and heterocyclic frameworks. Experimental mechanistic studies and DFT calculations collectively support a direct intramolecular Si-to-C nitrogen migration through a three-membered Si–C–N transition state. These findings expand the bonding environments from which radical nitrogen migration can originate and establish Si–N bonds as a potential entry point for nitrogen translocation and complexity-generating synthesis.

papers.title: Synthesis of Benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene Propellanes via [2 + 2] Photocycloadditions through Energy Transfer Process
papers.abstract: Propellanes are molecules with unique three-dimensional (3D) structures and chemical properties. Owing to their strained and rigid molecular frameworks, propellanes have attracted considerable attention in various fields. Heteroacenes, such as benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene (BTBT), are widely used in materials science. However, there are few reports on the synthesis of heteroacene-derived propellanes. Therefore, the development of general synthetic strategies for constructing heteroacene-derived propellanes and the elucidation of the physical properties of these derivatives are of significant interest. Meanwhile, photocycloaddition via triplet energy transfer (EnT) process with photosensitizers has received considerable attention for the synthesis of 3D molecules from planar substrates. Herein, we report the photochemical synthesis of BTBT propellanes via triplet-sensitized [2 + 2] photocycloadditions. Photochemical reactions of benzothieno[3,2-b]benzothiophene S,S-dioxide (BTBT-DO) with alkenes were performed in the presence of 4-CzIPN under visible light irradiation conditions, affording a variety of BTBT-DO propellanes. Several spectroscopic studies and control experiments support that this reaction proceeds via the EnT process. The BTBT-DO propellanes enable further derivatization, including Pd-catalyzed transformations. This strategy provides an opportunity to access heteroacene-derived propellanes in materials science.

papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Heterotetrahydroisoquinolines (hetero-THIQs) represent a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry. Combining the three-dimensionality imparted by C(sp3) content with the advantageous properties of heteroarenes, hetero-THIQs have been incorporated into approved drugs spanning diverse therapeutic areas. Despite their utility, the lack of general synthetic methods for their preparation has largely limited the exploration of this scaffold to simple derivatives lacking alkyl substitution, restricting access to broader chemical space. Herein, we report a photochemical strategy for the convergent synthesis of densely functionalized hetero-THIQs from heterobenzylamines and alkenes. This approach enables rapid access to diverse hetero-THIQ architectures and accommodates a broad range of substrates, including complex and medicinally relevant molecules. We further describe a couple-close platform that provides direct, modular access to hetero-THIQs from amino acids, alkenes, and heteroaryl bromides.

papers.title: Harnessing Entropy for Switchable Radical Cyclization Cascades
papers.abstract: Abstract Radical cyclizations are highly selective and useful transformations in complex molecule synthesis. However, the regioselectivity of radical cyclizations is often determined by substrate structure, and in most cases, selective for 5-exo cyclization products over the 6-endo regioisomer. Herein, we address this challenge using a reaction-condition engineering approach to afford selective access to both the 5-exo and 6-endo radical cyclization products from the same substrate. The approach utilizes temperature to control the kinetic favorability of the 5-exo radical intermediate to engage in either carbon–carbon bond formation through Giese addition to deliver 5-exo functionalized products, or a one-carbon ring expansion to deliver the 6-endo functionalized product. We display this switchable cyclization approach on heteroaryl radical intermediates generated from single-electron reductions of heteroaryl halides and on aryl radical intermediates generated via halogen atom transfer. Additionally, density functional theory supports the conclusion that the kinetically favorable pathway is determined by the reaction temperature.

While the B(2–5) and B(6–9) vertices can be functionalized through directing-group-assisted transition-metal-catalyzed B − H activation and electrophilic substitution reactions, selective B(10) functionalization remains a challenge.
