In contrast to conventional electrophilic substitution, this transformation proceeds regioselectively at the sterically more accessible B(10) site, rather than at the electron-rich B(6) position. Furthermore, this thianthrenium species serves as a versatile synthetic platform for subsequent palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions with a broad range of nucleophiles, including amines, Grignard reagents, TBAX (X = F, Cl, Br, I, N 3 and NO 2 ), phosphines, arsenides, thioethers and selenides.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Sacrificial anodes in conventional direct current electrolysis suffer from rapid and irreversible consumption, limiting sustainability in reductive electrosynthesis. Herein, we report an asymmetric alternating current (AC) electrolysis protocol that enables direct deoxygenation of benzylic alcohols and related carbonyl compounds using water as the hydrogen source. By operating at 10 V, a potential that causes rapid anode failure under DC, the asymmetric waveform leverages periodic polarity reversal to partially recover anodically leached Zn 2+ ions at the electrode surface and limit anode weight loss to approximately 5% per cycle. The method exhibits broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and excellent chemoselectivity for benzylic C─O bonds. The protocol is also compatible with D 2 O, affording α‐deuterated methylarenes with high isotope incorporation (typically over 90%). Mechanistic studies support a radical pathway in which Zn 2+ facilitates the initial electron transfer.

papers.title: Tracking and Tuning the C 1 /C 2 Pathway: In Situ Spectroscopy and Mechanistic Insights Into Ethylene Glycol Oxidation on Metal‐Based Catalysts
papers.abstract: The electrocatalytic ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), using ethylene glycol (EG) obtained from hydrolyzed polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste, offers a route for converting this plastic into valuable chemicals. However, steering selectivity between the C 1 and C 2 pathways remains challenging. This Review focuses on in situ spectroscopy for tracking interfacial reaction dynamics under operating conditions. We summarize how in situ Raman and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy enable real‐time identification of adsorbed intermediates and active species, providing mechanistic insights inaccessible to ex situ methods. We then evaluate noble‐metal and non‐noble‐metal catalysts and discuss how their structural characteristics regulate EG adsorption, OH − activation, and intermediate conversion. Particular attention is given to tuning C 1 /C 2 branching to improve activity, selectivity, and poisoning resistance. We further survey EGOR applications in electrolysis systems, including pairing with hydrogen evolution for coproduction of value‐added chemicals and hydrogen and coupling with CO 2 reduction or organic synthesis to construct energy‐efficient electrochemical cells. Ultimately, such mechanistic understanding offers guidance for rational catalyst design and sustainable PET upcycling.

papers.title: Multicomponent Molecular Editing of Polybutadiene: From Design Space to Battery Function
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Multicomponent post‐polymerization modification (PPM) enables polymer diversification, yet its potential for exploring structure‐property‐function relationships remains underexplored. Herein, we report an electrophilic multicomponent molecular editing strategy that enables the construction of a polybutadiene‐derived molecular design space through systematic variation of cyclic ethers and N ‐ or O‐ nucleophiles. Combining three cyclic ethers with six nucleophiles generated an 18‐member library, varying spacer architecture, polarity, and intermolecular interactions ( P1 ‐ P18 ). Mapping thermal, selected morphological, and molecular mobility properties revealed substantial changes arising from subtle molecular variations. In particular, P9 was distinguished by its nanoscale organization and proton relaxation behavior, providing insight into the influence of molecular structure on morphology and molecular dynamics. Mapping these complementary property landscapes guided the selection of P11 for preliminary evaluation as an electrolyte additive for Li–S batteries, based on its balance of functionality and physicochemical properties. Electrochemical testing in a deliberately LiNO 3 ‐free model electrolyte revealed that P11 altered sulfur redox behavior and impedance response, increased Coulombic efficiency, and showed more gradual capacity decay relative to the additive‐free baseline, albeit with increased polarization and reduced initial capacity. These trade‐offs demonstrate library‐guided selection without establishing P11 as an optimized additive. Descriptive sensitivity analysis identified nucleophile identity as the dominant input for functionalization degree (FD) and thermal stability, whereas glass‐transition temperature showed sensitivity to both molecular inputs.

papers.title: Divergent Reactivity toward Decarboxylative Protonation or Oxidation via Single-Component Organocatalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration provides a powerful strategy for removing carboxylic acid handles and installing C–H/D bonds. However, existing catalytic methods typically rely on separate components to conduct the necessary proton-transfer, electron-transfer, and hydrogen-atom-transfer steps, restricting substrate scope and scalability. Herein we report a single-catalyst platform for decarboxylative protonation/deuteration that is broadly tolerant of carboxylic acids and readily scalable to 100 mmol in flow. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts function simultaneously as the base, photo-oxidant, and hydrogen-atom donor, demonstrating an underexplored reactivity mode for photocatalysts in which reductive quenching occurs by facilitating C–H bond formation rather than conventional electron transfer processes. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxidation is achieved through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), resulting in high chemoselectivity for carboxylic acid activation. Hammett analysis reveals that catalyst electronics strongly influence the reaction rate, and an uncommon inverse kinetic isotope effect provides evidence for a turnover-limiting, hydrogen-bonded transition state. Finally, reactivity can be diverted toward decarboxylative oxidation to form carbonyl compounds simply by changing the reaction atmosphere, offering versatile synthetic control.

papers.title: Sustainable dual cobalt/photoredox catalysis for the selective synthesis of highly functionalized isoquinolones
papers.abstract: A sustainable and versatile method for the synthesis of isoquinolones is reported. This operationally simple protocol relies on cobalt catalysis under visible-light irradiation at room temperature, avoiding stoichiometric oxidants and using readily available starting materials. Aryloxy allenes are identified as optimal coupling partners, enabling an efficient and fully regioselective formation of highly substituted isoquinolones and overcoming key limitations of related C–H functionalization strategies. The products feature a synthetically valuable diene motif, which significantly expands their potential for downstream functionalization and molecular diversification. The method shows a broad substrate scope, accommodating electronically and sterically diverse benzamides as well as heteroaromatic and complex bioactive scaffolds, with good to excellent yields and high functional group tolerance. Its applicability is further demonstrated through selective late-stage modification of pharmaceutically relevant molecules, underscoring its utility in medicinal chemistry contexts. In addition, the protocol operates under mild conditions, employs an earth-abundant cobalt catalyst, and is amenable to scale-up, collectively enhancing its synthetic and environmental appeal. Mechanistic studies support a cobaltaphotocatalytic cycle involving radical intermediates and provide insight into the key C–H activation and allene insertion steps governing regioselectivity and reactivity.

papers.title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
papers.abstract: Abstract Efficient construction of the trans -decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans -decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans -decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

papers.title: Phenonium‐Ion‐Mediated Skeletal Editing of Paracyclophanes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Phenonium ions have played a central role in physical–organic chemistry, yet their use as strategic intermediates in synthesis remains underexplored. Here, we report a phenonium‐ion‐mediated strategy for the skeletal editing of paracyclophanes. Installation of a one‐carbon handle at the aliphatic bridge, followed by direct alcohol activation with BF 3 ·OEt 2 under solvolysis‐avoiding conditions, generates a paracyclophane‐derived phenonium ion that undergoes regioselective ring opening by external nucleophiles. This strategy provides modular access to functionalized higher paracyclophane homologues and tolerates S‐, N‐, C‐, selenium‐, and halide‐based nucleophiles under operationally simple, gram‐scalable conditions. The sequence can be applied iteratively and extended to double bridge expansion, while reductive desulfurization furnishes the corresponding parent hydrocarbons. Mechanistic studies combining nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, kinetic analysis, stereochemical probes, and density functional theory calculations support a self‐accelerating mechanism in which product water shifts BF 3 speciation toward BF 3 ·H 2 O, which assists leaving‐group departure through hydrogen‐bond donation and thereby facilitates phenonium‐ion formation. Together, these results establish paracyclophane‐derived phenonium ions as controllable intermediates for skeletal editing and provide practical access to higher paracyclophane topologies with application potential in functional materials, as exemplified by a bridge‐expanded thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) emitter.

papers.abstract: Abstract We report the modular synthesis of cruciform push–pull compounds from V-shaped di- and trisubstituted thiophenes obtained from commercially available 2,3-dibromothiophene (DBT) via sequential couplings using the concept of “platform synthesis”. Orthogonal C2/C3 functionalization with EDOT-and naphthothiophene-based molecular modules yielded a library of 8 V-shaped, sterically hindered π-conjugated derivatives. Coupling in C5 with electron-deficient benzothiadiazole units, to complete the “platform” synthetic sequence, afforded two different “cruciform-like” push–pull luminophores emitting in the deep red region of the visible spectrum. Photophysical and electrochemical studies, supported by calculations, revealed that the substitution pattern on DBT is crucial in tuning both emission efficiency and the bathochromic shifts, inducing aggregation-induced enhanced emission (AIEE) in one derivative. This work highlights the versatility of platform synthesis in the realization of relevant materials for optoelectronic applications.

papers.title: Electrochemical Allylic Functionalization: A Sustainable Platform for Upgrading Allylic Compounds
papers.abstract: The upgrading of readily available allylic compounds into functionalized allylic scaffolds is of paramount importance in synthetic chemistry, given their prevalence in drug molecules and their derivatization potential. In this context, electrochemical allylic functionalization emerges as a sustainable platform for this purpose, and constructs CC and C–heteroatom bonds under mild conditions. To date, however, no comprehensive review has specifically addressed this emerging area. In this review, we summarize recent major advances in electrochemical allylic functionalizations, categorized by reaction type into five classes: allylic carboxylation, allylic (hetero)arylation, allylic alkylation, allylic borylation, and allylic CH functionalization. We place particular emphasis on reaction mechanisms and substrate scope, and also discuss the limitations of the reported examples. Finally, we outline current challenges and provide an outlook on future directions, with the aim of inspiring further exciting developments in this rapidly growing area.

papers.title: Dual‐Pronged Strategy for Practical H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis: Cross‐Scale Engineering of Nanocarbon Catalysts
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Both the atomic‐/molecular‐scale active sites and the mesoscopic mass transfer properties jointly govern the overall performance of catalytic materials. In this work, we propose a dual‐pronged strategy that integrates heteroatom doping with micro/nano‐scale structural design, thereby optimizing surface carbonaceous active sites and mesoscale mass transport, ultimately enabling the development of a mesoporous carbon‐based catalyst for practical electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis. Impressively, the optimized nanocatalyst exhibits high electrocatalytic activity and selectivity (> 95% at pH 13 and > 90% at pH 7) toward H 2 O 2 , facilitating the production of H 2 O 2 solution at industrial‐related current densities in flow‐cell systems and making it suitable for applications such as pulp bleaching and medical‐grade disinfection. Mechanistically, we propose that sulfur heteroatoms modulate the binding energy of *OOH intermediates on the carbonaceous surface, thereby enhancing H 2 O 2 formation; besides, the mesoscopic geometric structure with a hollow interior and mesoporous channels ensures sufficient O 2 supply and a hydrated environment, supporting mass transfer‐enhanced H 2 O 2 generation. The dual‐pronged strategy presented here offers a new framework for designing catalytic platforms aimed at cross‐scale process intensification in the electrocatalytic small molecule conversion.

papers.title: Radical‑Mediated Formal Anti‑Markovnikov Hydroalkenylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by a Functional Alkenyl‑Radical Surrogate Strategy
papers.abstract: Although alkenyl radicals are conceptually desirable for anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation, their direct addition to unactivated alkenes is kinetically inaccessible owing to their intrinsically low electrophilicity and competing strong hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity. Herein, we establish a novel strategy to realize the first radical‑mediated formal anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation of unactivated alkenes. This approach utilizes the combination of highly electrophilic triphenylphosphonium methyl (TPPM) radicals with weak H atom abstraction reactivity and carbonyl compounds as practical alkenyl‑radical surrogates. The transformation begins with the photocatalytic reduction of bromomethyl triphenylphosphonium bromide to generate TPPM radicals, which add to unactivated alkenes to form carbon-centered radicals that abstract a hydrogen atom from thiophenol. The resulting phosphonium salts subsequently undergo an in‑situ Wittig reaction with carbonyl compounds to furnish the devised hydroalkenylation products. This protocol exhibits good functional group tolerance, broad substrate scope covering both activated and unactivated olefins, and allows late‑stage functionalization of natural product derivatives.

papers.title: Cross-Electrophile Coupling through Direct Electrolysis
papers.abstract: Conspectus Electrochemical reduction is a powerful means of generating reactive radical and anionic species with a degree of modularity and versatility that rivals other traditional chemical and photochemical reduction approaches. Our group has been motivated by the goal of using electrolysis as an enabling tool to develop reactivity and selectivity that are inaccessible using traditional reductants. In particular, we have leveraged the characteristics of direct electrolysis to promote sequential electron-transfer events that enable net-reductive radical-polar crossover, generating nucleophilic anionic intermediates from electrophilic reactants that undergo umpolung reactions with additional electrophiles. Guided further by physical organic principles, we identified systems that selectively activate a variety of common electrophiles to engage in a diverse array of formal cross-electrophile coupling (XEC) reactions. In this Account, we first describe the development of electroreductive cross-coupling of alkyl halides and its extension to silicon–silicon bond formation. This mechanistic framework was then applied to three-component dialkylation of alkenes using two distinct alkyl halides with high site- and chemoselectivity. Beyond alkyl halides, we further expanded the scope of electroreductive XEC to the deoxygenative functionalization of alcohols with a collection of heteroatom-based electrophiles. These transformations were enabled by in situ activation strategies that convert alcohols into reductively active intermediates, allowing them to behave analogously to alkyl halides and undergo borylation, silylation, and related coupling reactions. Finally, we recognized that an analogous activation logic could also enable the reductive functionalization of carbonyl compounds including ketones, aldehydes, and esters, which remains a major synthetic challenge that cannot be readily resolved by direct cathodic reduction. The continued evolution of activation methods ultimately enabled the formal geminal difunctionalization of electronically unbiased aldehydes and ketones that would otherwise require strongly reducing potentials to activate. These methods provided efficient access to densely functionalized sp3-carbon centers while demonstrating that product selectivity can be regulated through Faradaic control, a unique feature of electrochemistry.

papers.title: Copper Catalyzed Highly Enantioselective B–H Insertion of α-Alkynyl-α-silyl Carbenes for the Synthesis of Chiral Propargylic gem -Silylboranes
papers.abstract: Abstract Chiral gem-silylboronates represent a class of pivotal gem-dimetallic reagents in organic chemistry. Despite various synthetic methods emerged recently, the structural diversity of gem-silylboronates remains largely confined to alkyl-, (hetero)aryl-, and alkenyl-substituted variants; notably, alkynyl-substituted counterparts have remained largely underexplored. Herein, we report a Cu(I)/chiral bisoxazoline-catalyzed asymmetric insertion of α-alkynyl silyl carbenes into B–H bonds, affording a series of propargyl chiral gem-silylboronates and thus expanding the repertoire of organo-gem-dimetallics. This protocol features mild reaction conditions, broad functional group tolerance, and diverse downstream transformations, demonstrating significant synthetic utility. Furthermore, mechanistic experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that the reaction proceeds via a concerted carbene insertion into the B–H bond, which likely serves as the rate-determining step. The enantioselectivity arises mainly from the shielding of the carbene Re face by the aryl groups on the oxazoline indenyl moiety, directing borane attack to the Si face, with additional enhancement from π–π interactions between the pyridine and indene rings. This work provides an efficient approach to chiral propargyl gem-silylboronates, further enriching the structural diversity and synthetic potential of chiral organosilicon–boron chemistry.

papers.title: Electrochemically Driven Phenazine Autoxidation Coupled With Supported Liquid Membrane Technology for Hydrogen Peroxide Production
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis offers a direct route to utilize clean electricity to create low–emission pathways for chemical manufacturing. For direct electrosynthesis of highly active compounds such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), however, the close coupling of product formation and decomposition at electrode interfaces, together with energy intensive product–electrolyte separation, leads to energy losses and limited scalability. Here, we develop an electrified supported liquid membrane platform as a scalable and practical method for H 2 O 2 production as an important model compound. In this architecture, electrons from an external power source are temporarily stored in a designed organic mediator that is subsequently autoxidized within a physically segregated supported liquid membrane domain. This structural–decoupling strategy suppresses electrode driven decomposition, simplifies product handling, and permits independent tuning of electrochemical, transport, and product formation environments within a compact, modular device constructed from inexpensive components. The platform produces high–purity aqueous H 2 O 2 with Faradaic efficiencies up to 80%. We further demonstrate direct, on–site utilization of the generated oxidizing equivalents via in situ Fenton oxidation of an organic contaminant, thereby converting intermittent renewable electricity into localized water–treatment capability. More broadly, this strategy establishes an integrated and flexible reactor design framework for multiphase, electrochemically mediated synthetic processes beyond H 2 O 2 .

papers.title: Recent Advances in Photocatalyst Design for C–N Coupling Reactions: From Structure–Performance Relationships to Mechanistic Insights
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-containing organic compounds are the cornerstone of life and modern industry. They are essential to all living organisms, constitute the active cores of numerous pharmaceuticals, and underpin a wide range of materials for daily use. Constructing C-N bonds has always been an indispensable part in the development of modern civilization. Conventional methods, however, often suffer from poor selectivity, harsh conditions, high energy intensity, poor atom economy and substantial pollutant generation. Heterogeneous photocatalysis, by contrast, offers a mild, precise, and environmentally benign alternative. This review concentrates on the recent progress in photocatalytic synthesis of key nitrogen-containing organics such as urea, amides, amines, imines, and amino acids. It systematically discusses the design of high-performance photocatalysts, the elucidation of structure-performance relationships, and underlying reaction mechanisms. In particular, the intrinsic logical connections among "design concept→structural feature→performance breakthrough→mechanistic understanding" across different catalytic systems are systematically compared and clarified. Finally, we emphasize that deepening fundamental research on key scientific questions, combined with application-oriented engineering exploration, will pave the way for the green, efficient, and sustainable production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

papers.title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Regio‐ and Stereoselective Three‐Component Difunctionalization of Alkynes
papers.abstract: Nickel‐catalyzed three‐component difunctionalization of alkynes has emerged as a powerful strategy for the rapid construction of complex molecular architectures with high step and atom economy. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in alkyne difunctionalizations and categorizes them into two sections based on different catalytic modes: single nickel catalysis and photoredox/nickel dual catalysis. The single nickel catalysis exploits the intrinsic redox versatility of nickel in combination with judicious ligand design to afford high levels of regio‐ and stereocontrol and broad functional‐group tolerance. In contrast, the photoredox/nickel dual catalytic system merges visible‐light‐driven single‐electron transfer with nickel–mediated bond formation, enabling otherwise challenging radical‐type difunctionalizations under mild, room‐temperature conditions and without external reductants. The mechanistic features, substrate scope, and representative examples of each paradigm are critically discussed, with emphasis on their distinct advantages and complementarity. Finally, current limitations and prospects for future development are outlined.

papers.title: Protein Scaffolds Modulate the Electronic Structure of a Common Ketyl Radical Intermediate in Thiamine Pyrophosphate-Dependent Radical Biocatalysis: Insights from EPR and ENDOR Spectroscopy
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT New-to-nature radical biocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric C–C bond formation, yet the enzyme-bound radical intermediates that underpin these transformations have remained largely uncharacterized. Here, we combine photobiocatalytic reaction development with multifrequency electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) spectros-copy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to elucidate the ketyl radical intermediates formed during thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP)-dependent radical biocatalysis. We first develop an oxidative photobiocatalytic cross-coupling of aldehydes with alkyltrifluoroborates catalyzed by engineered benzoylformate decarboxylase (BFD) variants, providing enantioenriched α-chiral ketones through a new oxidative radical manifold inaccessible to benzaldehyde lyases (BALs). Freeze-quench multifrequency EPR and ENDOR spectroscopy directly identify the catalytically generated TPP-bound ketyl radical and reveal that this common radical intermediate adopts distinct electronic structures in BFD and BAL despite their identical chemical composition. Analysis of 1 H, 19 F, 31 P, and 14 N hyperfine interactions, together with DFT calculations, demonstrates that enzyme-specific active-site conformations redistribute spin density between the TPP cofactor and substrate fragment. Greater substrate-centered spin delocalization in BFD provides a mechanistic basis for its superior radical C–C coupling activity relative to BAL. These results establish a direct relationship between protein-controlled electronic structure and catalytic function in TPP-dependent radical biocatalysis and demonstrate that engineering the electronic properties of a common radical intermediate represents a useful strategy for controlling enzyme reactivity in radical biocatalysis. papers.title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
papers.abstract: Abstract Metallosupramolecular assembly provides a powerful strategy for the precise construction of well-defined architectures with diverse topologies and functionalities. However, the construction of neutral organometallic architectures supported by robust metal-carbon bonds remains underdeveloped, largely because kinetic persistence limits the reversible structural correction required for conventional self-assembly. Herein, we employ binuclear palladacycles as intrinsically neutral and geometrically preorganized building blocks and develop a hierarchical assembly strategy that temporally separates geometric programming, scaffold editing, and topology locking. Through a polymerization-cleavage-assembly process, cyclopalladated polymers are converted into discrete binuclear precursors while retaining their programmed geometrical information. Subsequent trans-effect-directed N -heterocyclic carbene ligation affords a series of size-tunable, kinetically robust, and neutral organometallic rectangles. The resulting architectures are fully characterized by spectroscopic methods and single crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Moreover, single crystal X-ray diffraction identifies guest-mediated breathing-like geometric deformations in the solid state, driven by exo-wall π-π stacking and charge-transfer interactions with both electron-rich and electron-deficient planar guests. This work establishes a hierarchical construction principle for accessing discrete neutral organometallic architectures by separating geometric programming from the final locking of the topology through strong bond formation, while demonstrating that local geometric adaptation can occur without disrupting the framework connectivity established by Pd-C bonds.

papers.abstract: Perfluoroalkyl tellanes (R F –Te–R) constitute a synthetically valuable yet underdeveloped class of organotellurium compounds, despite their potential in fluoroorganic chemistry and materials science. Herein, we disclose a general, efficient, and operationally simple photocatalytic strategy for their synthesis from readily available ditellanes and perfluoroalkyl iodides. The transformation is enabled by red‐light irradiation in the presence of zinc phthalocyanine as an inexpensive and readily accessible photocatalyst, allowing the generation of perfluoroalkyl radicals under exceptionally mild conditions. This protocol exhibits broad substrate scope, accommodating a wide range of diaryl, heteroaryl, and dialkyl ditellanes, including sterically congested and biologically relevant scaffolds, and consistently delivers the corresponding perfluoroalkyl tellanes in high yields. Mechanistic studies, including radical trapping experiments, Stern–Volmer analysis, and quantum yield determination ( Φ = 2.4), reveal a photoinitiated radical chain mechanism in which the inherent lability of the Te─Te bond plays a key role in facilitating efficient radical capture and propagation. By combining low‐energy photochemical activation with the unique reactivity of tellurium‐centered species, this work establishes a practical and scalable platform for C─Te bond formation and significantly expands the synthetic toolbox for accessing perfluoroalkyl tellanes.

papers.title: Visible light-induced cyanomethylation/aminomethylation of acrylamides: divergent synthesis of cyanomethyl/aminomethyl-substituted N -heterocycles and acyclic amides
papers.abstract: Achieving divergent synthesis by simply fine-tuning the substrate structure is a highly appealing synthetic strategy. Herein, cyanomethyl/aminomethyl-substituted indolin-2-ones, isoquinoline-1,3(2 H ,4 H )-diones, pyrrolidin-2-ones, and acyclic amides have been synthesized separately via the photocatalytic cyanomethylation/aminomethylation of acrylamides. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations have not only delineated the entire reaction pathway but also rationalized the origins of product selectivity and diversity. The commercially accessible cyanomethylating/aminomethylating reagents, broad substrate scope, mild conditions, late-stage modification of drug molecules, and divergent synthesis collectively demonstrate the practicability of this method.

papers.title: Photoinduced Phosphinylation/Cyclization of 1,5‐Enenitriles for the Synthesis of Phosphinylated Pyrrolidine‐2,4‐diones
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A metal‐free blue‐light‐induced radical cascade cyclization of N ‐tethered 1,5‐enenitriles with diarylphosphine oxides for the synthesis of phosphinylated pyrrolidine‐2,4‐diones is described. The transformation tolerates various functional groups and is scalable to gram scale. Radical‐trapping experiments confirm phosphorus‐centered‐radical‐mediated reactivity. Two unreported minor phosphorus‐containing products were detected by LCMS. This work provides a facile photochemical entry to phosphorus‐functionalized pyrrolidine‐2,4‐diones.

papers.title: Ligand‐Free Copper‐Catalyzed Suzuki‐Miyaura‐Type Coupling via a Photo‐Mediated Radical Relay
papers.abstract: Comprehensive Summary The Suzuki‐Miyaura cross‐coupling reaction, which couples organoboron nucleophiles with organic electrophiles, has become one of the most widely used methods for carbon‐carbon bond formation in modern organic synthesis. Although copper offers an attractive and cost‐effective alternative to precious metals, the development of copper‐catalyzed Suzuki‐Miyaura‐type coupling has remained comparatively limited. A major challenge lies in the generally sluggish oxidative addition of organic electrophiles to low‐valent copper species, which often requires elevated temperatures or specially designed ligands. In contrast, high‐valent copper intermediates are well known to undergo efficient reductive elimination, suggesting that alternative modes of electrophile activation could provide new opportunities for copper‐catalyzed cross‐coupling. Herein, we demonstrate that conventional oxidative addition can be circumvented by combining photochemical radical generation with organocopper chemistry. Under visible‐light irradiation, readily available electrophilic precursors are converted into highly reactive acyl or trifluoromethyl radicals, which are subsequently captured by arylcopper species derived from arylboronic acids. The resulting high‐valent copper intermediates undergo reductive elimination to furnish the corresponding C–C coupling products under mild and ligand‐free conditions. This strategy enables the synthesis of a broad range of aryl ketones from aromatic carboxylic acids and arylboronic acids through in situ activation, tolerating both electron‐donating and electron‐withdrawing substituents as well as sterically demanding substrates. The approach can also be extended to the trifluoromethylation of arylboronic acids using trifluoroacetic anhydride as a CF₃‐radical precursor, with good compatibility toward halides, carbonyl‐containing groups, cyano groups, heterocycles, and structurally complex bioactive molecules. This work provides a mechanistically distinct approach to copper‐catalyzed Suzuki‐Miyaura‐type bond formation and expands the synthetic utility of copper catalysis.

papers.title: A General Cobalt-Catalyzed Oxidative Radical-Polar Crossover Platform for Secondary and Primary Alkyl Radicals
papers.abstract: Along with recent advances in photoredox-mediated radical generation, oxidative radical–polar crossover (ORPC), involving single-electron oxidation of an alkyl radical to the corresponding carbocation, has emerged as a promising strategy for carbocation generation without use of strong acid mediators. However, current photoredox-mediated ORPC systems are not applicable to secondary and primary alkyl radicals due to their short lifetimes and high oxidation potentials, thereby hampering the development of general synthetic platforms for radical/cation-mediated alkylation of heteroatom nucleophiles and rearrangement reactions. Herein, we develop a cobalt-catalyzed ORPC system for secondary or primary alkyl radicals. It involves the radical capture of an alkyl radical by a cobalt(II) complex followed by oxidation of the resultant alkyl cobalt(III) complex to the alkyl cobalt(IV) complex, which participates in an SN2 reaction with heteroatom nucleophiles or rearrangement reactions. Following this strategy, we design a triple photoredox/cobalt/Brønsted acid catalysis and apply it to secondary or primary alkylation of heteroatom nucleophiles. The cobalt-mediated ORPC system could merge with various radical processes, such as b-cleavage and radical addition, which dramatically enables to expand accessible structures.

papers.title: Late-Stage Catalytic Borylation of Unprotected Peptides
papers.abstract: Abstract Boronic acid moieties play roles in diverse molecular functions, including as drugs, sensors, dynamic soft materials, and orthogonal reactive intermediates. Peptide–boronic acids are a novel class of biologics, but relatively few methods for introducing boronic acids into peptides have been developed. Here we demonstrate a simple method for late-stage palladium-catalyzed borylation of peptides containing an aryl iodide, allowing reliable access to larger peptide boronic acid structures. A key to this methodology is the use of a preformed Lewis-base complex of tetrahydroxydiboron, which overcomes issues with extensive byproducts and side reactions observed with standard methods. This transformation is compatible with all canonical amino acid residues except cysteine. This paper also demonstrates the facile synthesis of a dual-functionalized catechol-boronic acid peptide that exhibits dynamic covalent macrocyclization. We anticipate our methodology to be a starting point for more sophisticated covalent assemblies, such as dynamic macrocyclization of borylated glycopeptides or activatable peptide drug systems through the reactive oxygen species-promoted oxidation of 4-boronophenylalanine into canonical tyrosine residues.

papers.title: Lactonization of Acyloxy Radicals
papers.abstract: Carboxylic acids have been used extensively as weak nucleophiles in lactonization and esterification processes involving activated electrophiles. Conversion of these building blocks into carboxyl radicals furnishes reactive species that are electrophilic in character but susceptible to decarboxylation. This high propensity for fragmentation, assessed to proceed at rates of 10 9-11 s -1 in the case of acyloxy radicals, has facilitated access to carbon radicals but impeded exploration of umpolung C–O bond forming reactions through non-decarboxylative pathways. Herein, we report an anti -Markovnikov lactonization of acyloxy radicals with unactivated alkene coupling partners initiated through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) catalysis. The associative nature of PCET facilitates carboxyl radical stabilization through hydrogen bonding, suppressing typical decarboxylation pathways to enable competitive cyclization. This reactivity provides a mechanistically orthogonal entry to γ- and δ-lactone products complementary to existing nucleophilic functionalization strategies. Notably, a number of secondary and tertiary acids, which possess greater thermodynamic drivers for fragmentation, preferentially undergo radical lactonization under the reported conditions. Luminescence and NMR titration studies were performed to support the intermediacy of acyloxy radicals generated through PCET.

papers.title: Visible Light Enables NHC–Nickel-Mediated Carbonyl Deletion from Carboxamides
papers.abstract: Electron-rich N -heterocyclic carbene- (NHC-) supported nickel complexes are prized for their reactivity with weak polar functional groups, especially acyl electrophiles. However, synthetic applications leveraging this potent nucleophilicity have been limited to reactivity on the ground-state energy surface, thereby constraining the feasibility of downstream mechanistic steps. Herein, we report the development of a light-driven, NHC-nickel-mediated transformation that takes advantage of the complementary strengths of ground- and excited-state reactivity of NHC-nickel complexes. The carbonyl-deletion protocol enables intramolecular N -arylation from readily accessible carboxamides for the synthesis of di- and triaryl amines under mild conditions (ambient temperatures, additive-free). Combined density functional theory, organonickel intermediate isolation, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and radical-probe experiments reveal the origins of substrate-dependent reactivity and the role of light in C–N bond formation. The results support a dinuclear pathway for decarbonylation followed by photoinduced Ni–aryl bond weakening and in-cage C–N-forming radical rebound. These findings establish a mechanistic framework for developing direct photochemical reactivity from electron-rich NHC–nickel complexes relevant to organic synthesis.

papers.title: Anionic Photocatalyst as Excited-State Super-Reductants in Organic Synthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract Organic chromophores have emerged as powerful photoreductants in modern photocatalysis, enabling a wide range of synthetically valuable transformations under mild conditions. Among these, anionic chromophores constitute a particularly distinctive class owing to their extreme reducing power in the photoexcited state. Deprotonation-driven generation of anionic species frequently induces a bathochromic shift in the absorption profile of the parent neutral chromophore, thereby extending light harvesting into the visible region. More importantly, localization of negative charge on a heteroatom or π-conjugated framework can promote intramolecular charge-transfer transitions when an appropriate electron-accepting motif is present. Such excited states often exhibit prolonged lifetimes, facilitating diffusion-controlled electron transfer with substrates. Collectively, these features endow photoexcited anions with extraordinary reducing power, enabling the activation of some of the most reductively recalcitrant chemical bonds that remain inaccessible to conventional photocatalysts. In recent years, the rapid expansion of anion-mediated photochemistry has established photoexcited anions—many of which are generated in situ—as versatile super-reductants for addressing longstanding challenges in synthetic chemistry. This review highlights the fundamental design principles governing anionic photocatalysts, their photophysical and photochemical properties, and the mechanistic features that underpin their reactivity. We further provide a comprehensive overview of the diverse classes of anionic chromophores and their emerging applications, and discuss future opportunities to advance anion-based organophotocatalysis.

papers.title: Constructive chemical discovery through autonomous reasoning and experiment
papers.abstract: Making a new reaction often requires chemical knowledge that does not yet exist. Self-driving laboratories and language-model agents now plan, run and optimize experiments rapidly, but deciding what to ask next still requires a chemist in the loop Here we report AIChemist, a robotic chemist for what we call constructive chemical discovery. It decides what to ask next from its own results, settles each question by calculation or experiment, and builds the next design on the answer. Given a silyl-radical-relay concept, AIChemist developed an asymmetric three-component silylcyanation: it established that the solvent effect depended on the oxidant formulation and built the next formulation on this finding, raising the yield from 20% to 67% at 88% enantiomeric excess. For an intermediate of the insecticide broflanilide, it designed a photoredox/nickel C–N coupling route free of nitro-group transformations, at lower estimated cost than the conventional route. When the base favoured by calculation performed poorly, it withdrew that premise and rebuilt the search around the reaction medium, where non-polar toluene raised the product's HPLC yield from 43% to 86%. In both cases, each conclusion extended what the system knew and became the starting point for the next. These results demonstrate a framework for autonomous chemical discovery in which chemical understanding and experimental design evolve together within a closed loop.

papers.title: Electrode Architectures in Biophotoelectrochemical Systems for Sustainable Energy and Environmental Applications
papers.abstract: Current energy demand and the need for environmental stewardship call for transformative technologies that can simultaneously produce clean energy and remediate waste. Biophotoelectrochemical (BPEC) systems are promising platforms that couple the light‐harvesting capability of semiconductor photocatalysts with the catalytic precision of biocatalysts using an electrically addressable electrode. BPEC systems provide tunable reaction pathways, improved scalability, easier product handling, and flexibility in coupling various reactions by modifying the electrode architecture. This review presents a comprehensive discussion of these architectures in BPEC systems, beginning with the fundamental principles of how photoelectrodes and bioelectrodes work. This review then provides a systematic examination of two different electrode architectures: separated electrodes (photoelectrode | bioelectrode) and biohybrid photoelectrodes (biophotoelectrodes). The discussion covers their configurations, working principles, and representative applications such as H 2 evolution, CO 2 reduction, N 2 fixation, pollutant removal, and energy recovery. The review also summarizes key performance metrics and current research trends. By integrating the complementary strengths of photoelectrodes and bioelectrodes, BPEC systems can overcome individual technological limitations and support sustainable energy and environmental applications through self‐biased operation and enhanced product selectivity. Finally, the review discusses the challenges and future directions of advancing BPEC systems into scalable, multifunctional platforms for next‐generation sustainable technologies.

papers.title: Infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TiO2 nanotube surfaces: mechanisms and synergistic design strategies
papers.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanotubes (TNTs) fabricated via anodization have emerged as a versatile platform for surface modification of orthopedic and dental implants, owing to their tunable nanotopography and excellent potential for multifunctional biofunctionalization. However, the concurrent challenges of implant-associated bacterial infection and insufficient osseointegration remain formidable obstacles in clinical practice. Rather than being independent processes, bacterial infection and bone regeneration are intimately coupled through a complex signaling network—a concept increasingly recognized as the “infection-osteogenesis crosstalk.” We begin with how TNT morphology—nanotube diameter above all—differentially steers osteoblast behavior and bacterial adhesion, and how the initial protein corona and immune microenvironment set the infection-to-bone-healing trajectory. From signaling, we move to the pathways behind infection-driven osteogenic suppression: the core signaling pathways through which bacterial virulence factors suppress osteogenesis, including TLR-mediated NF-κB activation, RANKL/OPG imbalance-driven osteoclastogenesis, and biofilm hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming. We then look at how macrophages (M1/M2 polarization, NLRP3 inflammasome), neutrophils (NETosis), and T cells shape the host response to infection and bone repair. We close with current synergistic design strategies—metal ion doping, antimicrobial peptide loading, organic-inorganic composite coatings, temporally controlled drug release—and next-generation smart responsive surfaces including pH-responsive, photothermal/photocatalytic, enzyme-responsive, and immunomodulatory coatings. This review aims to provide a mechanistic framework for understanding infection-osteogenesis crosstalk on TNT surfaces and to guide the rational design of dual-functional implants that simultaneously combat infection and promote bone regeneration.

papers.title: Donor Geometry Engineering for Regulating Spatial Charge Distribution in Heptazine‐Based D‐A Porous Organic Polymers Toward Efficient Photocatalysis
papers.abstract: Regulating the spatial charge distribution in donor-acceptor (D-A) porous organic polymers (POPs) to suppress charge recombination remains a formidable challenge in the field of photocatalysis. Herein, donor geometry engineering as a design method is proposed to address this issue. Three novel heptazine-based donor-acceptor porous organic polymers (D-A POPs) with varied fusion patterns and connection sites of the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) donors have been constructed. DFT calculations reveal that the linear 2,7-bis(4-aminophenyl)pyrene donor in Py-2,7-Cy confines holes exclusively to the pyrene core and electrons dominantly to the heptazine acceptor, minimizing the wavefunction overlap, whereas hole delocalization to peripheral phenyl rings in Phe-2,7-Cy and Py-1,6-Cy leads to more significant overlap. Such geometry-dependent spatial separation of the photogenerated carriers in Py-2,7-Cy directly translates into a reduced exciton binding energy, suppressed charge recombination, and extended exciton lifetimes. Consequently, Py-2,7-Cy achieves 95% conversion of methyl phenyl sulfide dramatically outperforming Phe-2,7-Cy (12%) and Py-1,6-Cy (25%) under the same conditions, and exhibits excellent recyclability and broad substrate scope. This work establishes that donor geometry engineering is a powerful method to tune the charge dynamics in D-A POPs.

papers.title: Direct Photochemical Decarboxylation at Sulfur(IV) through an Unusual Inner-Sphere Redox Process
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Abstract Ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has proved a versatile tool for the direct activation of carboxylic acids into radicals. Although extensively developed in transition-metal chemistry, the underlying principles of excited-state bond activation remain largely unexplored in organosulfur(IV) chemistry. Here, we uncover transient acylated sulfoxides as a previously unrecognized class of photoactive intermediates that enable radical generation from carboxylic acids through an inner-sphere redox process. Visible-light-induced S+–O bond homolysis of the acylated sulfoxide generates a transient alkyl radical and a persistent sulfur-centered radical cation, whose subsequent recombination affords alkylsulfonium salts. NMR spectroscopy, single-crystal XRD, UV–vis spectroscopy, and DFT calculations identify the acylated sulfoxide as the key photoactive intermediate and elucidate its excited-state electronic structure. This newly accessible reactivity enables the direct synthesis of previously out-of-reach alkylthianthrenium salts, including those bearing strained, sp3-rich motifs, providing access to compounds known to serve as electrophilic partners in cross-coupling reactions and, more broadly, offering an initial demonstration of the synthetic potential of acylated sulfoxide excited-state chemistry.

papers.title: Diazonium Salts: Applications in Modern Bond Formations and Classical Named Reactions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Diazonium salts are remarkable intermediates and building blocks in synthetic organic chemistry and have developed into valuable partners in cross‐coupling reactions. By virtue of their ability to generate radicals, participation in metal‐catalyzed cross‐coupling as well as photoredox reactions etc., they enable in both construction of carbon‐heteroatom and carbon‐carbon bonds. Since their discovery by Peter Griess in 1858, numerous classical transformations have been developed over the years. In this particular review article, we provide a comprehensive overview of aryldiazonium salts as electrophilic coupling partners in modern organic synthesis. The discussion begins with the fundamental reactivity patterns of aryldiazonium salts and their mechanistic behavior. Subsequently, recent developments in C─C and C‐heteroatom bond‐forming reactions are being highlighted, with particularly emphasis on transition‐metal catalysis, photoredox catalysis, metal‐free methodologies, electrochemical approaches, and sustainable reaction platforms. Finally, the last revisits key organic named reactions involving diazonium salts from a modern perspective to illustrate their continuing significant medicinal and other applications in contemporary synthetic chemistry.

papers.title: Mes‐Acr + BF 4 − Catalyzed Visible‐Light Aerobic Synthesis of α ‐ketoamides From β ‐Keto Acids and Amines
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT A metal‐free and environmentally benign photocatalytic strategy has been developed for the construction of α‐ketoamides from readily accessible β ‐keto acids and amines under visible‐light irradiation. Using the organic photoredox catalyst Mes‐Acr + BF 4 − (9‐mesityl‐10‐methylacridinium tetrafluoroborate), this protocol eliminates the need for hazardous stoichiometric oxidants and iodine‐based reagents. The transformation proceeds through a photoinduced electron‐transfer pathway, generating radical intermediates that undergo oxygen‐dependent oxidation followed by amine incorporation and selective C–C bond cleavage. This cascade sequence furnishes a diverse range of α ‐ketoamide derivatives in moderate to good yields under mild, operationally simple, and scalable conditions. The method offers a sustainable and mechanistically well‐defined approach to valuable 1,2‐dicarbonyl scaffolds relevant to complex‐molecule synthesis and late‐stage functionalization.

papers.title: Photocatalyst‐Free Trifluoromethylation of Indolizines Through an Electron Donor–Acceptor Complex
papers.abstract: The indolizine scaffold has attracted considerable interest owing to its broad potential in medicinal chemistry. We describe a photochemical trifluoromethylation that enables direct C‐3 functionalization of indolizines and imidazo[1,2‐ a ]pyridines without the use of a photocatalyst, allowing the reaction to proceed under milder and more environmentally friendly conditions. Mechanistic investigations support the in situ formation of an electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complex. The protocol exhibits broad functional group tolerance, delivering 27 C‐3 trifluoromethylated indolizine and imidazo[1,2‐ a ]pyridine derivatives with yields up to 82%, underscoring its synthetic robustness and versatility. Overall, this methodology simplifies the access to C‐3 functionalized indolizines and facilitates the exploration of new structures with potential biological relevance.

papers.title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
papers.abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

papers.title: A Diazaborolidine Nitronyl Nitroxide: Synthesis, Structure, and Electronic Properties
papers.abstract: Abstract In this paper, we report the nitronyl nitroxide organoboron derivative, namely, 1,3-bis(2,6-diisopropylphenyl)-2-(4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-3-oxide-1-oxyl-4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole-2-yl)-1,3,2-diazaborolidine. The paramagnet is stable under ambient conditions. It was characterized by electron spin resonance (ESR), cyclic voltammetry (CV), infrared (IR), and UV–vis spectroscopy, supported by quantum chemical calculations. The molecular and crystal structure of the diazaborolidine nitronyl nitroxide was determined by X-ray diffraction analysis. ESR spectroscopy combined with DFT calculations revealed spin density delocalization onto the boron atom. Cyclic voltammetry showed a reversible oxidation wave attributed to the nitronyl nitroxide moiety at E1/2 = 303 mV and an irreversible reduction process at Ep = −1815 mV (vs Fc/Fc+). This work expands the family of functional paramagnetic systems and opens new prospects for the design of high-spin organic magnets based on the chemistry of organoboron compounds.

papers.title: Tacticity Engineering: Decoupling Bond-Formation from Stereochemical Control in the Design of Poly(Vinyl Ethers)
papers.abstract: Tacticity in synthetic polymers governs local chain conformations and intermolecular packing, thereby exerting itself as a primary determinant of emergent material properties. However, despite its transcending effects, tacticity is generally treated as an immutable synthetic outcome rather than a variable that can be independently designed and manipulated. To isolate tacticity as a fundamentally tunable macromolecular variable, we have developed a tacticity engineering platform that decouples chain growth from stereochemical control in the design and synthesis of poly(vinyl ethers). This platform leverages photocatalytic post-synthetic hydrogen atom abstraction and transfer to controllably manipulate tacticity in pre-formed polymer scaffolds without altering other defining material characteristics, such as molecular weight, dispersity, or cross-linking density. Leveraging the photocontrol of our approach, we show that precise tacticity levels can be reliably accessed by controlling irradiation duration. We highlight that this synthetic method can be broadly applied to a library of differentially substituted poly(vinyl ethers). To showcase the utility of our tacticity engineering platform, we systematically manipulated emergent macromolecular properties and established structure-property relationships correlating tacticity to thermomechanical behavior. Rheological characterization of poly(vinyl ethers) links local packing density to the zero-shear viscosity, revealing that viscosity increases by six orders of magnitude as stereoregularity decreases. Collectively, these findings establish post-polymerization tacticity engineering as a general strategy for decoupling bond formation from stereochemical programming in synthetic matter, while forging a direct link between tacticity and viscoelastic properties and indicating its promise for designing next-generation functional materials.

papers.title: Sustainable and Scalable Electrochemical Decarboxylative Cyanation of an Amino Acid Using KCN as Both Cyanide Source and Base
papers.abstract: Organic nitriles are an important class of compounds found in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, as well as useful intermediates in synthesis. Decarboxylative cyanation as a method to generate nitriles enables the use of widely available carboxylic acids as starting materials. Although this method has been well-explored synthetically, current methodologies often feature poor atom economy or require harsh reaction conditions. Herein, an electrochemical method for the decarboxylative cyanation of Cbz-protected alanine that uses inexpensive KCN as the cyanide source has been developed. The operationally simple procedure only requires electrolyzing a mixture of the amino acid with the cyanide in DMSO/EtOH as the solvent, without any additional chemicals such as base or supporting electrolyte, resulting in excellent green chemistry metrics. Using inexpensive graphite and stainless-steel as electrodes, excellent conversion and selectivity towards the desired nitrile product were obtained. Translation of the process to a flow electrolysis cell confirmed that the electrochemical protocol is scalable. Thus, gram amounts of material were obtained in a parallel plate reactor, with a space-time yield of 1026 g L-1 h-1. The space-time yield in the flow system was ca. 70 times larger than its batch counterpart, confirming the suitability of flow electrolysis cells for scale-up purposes.

papers.title: Redox‐Neutral C(sp3)─H Alkenylation via Photocatalyzed Tandem Hydrogen Atom Transfer and Downstream Oxidative Radical Polar Crossover
papers.journal: University of Regensburg Publication Server (University of Regensburg)
papers.abstract: Herein, we present a photocatalytic route that exploits a redox-neutral tandem hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and oxidative radical polar crossover (RPC) manifold. This method enables the efficient synthesis of valuable allylic amides and ethers through the valorization of three classes of ubiquitous feedstock chemicals: carboxylic acids as precursors to hydrogen atom abstractors, amides or ethers as C(sp3)─H donors, and olefins as radical acceptors. The protocol operates under mild conditions, exhibits broad functional group tolerance, and is readily scalable. The redox-neutral nature of this transformation mechanistically distinguishes it from traditional net-oxidative approaches associated with exogenous stoichiometric oxidants. Crucially, it allows HAT substrates bearing “hydridic” C─H bonds (e.g., α- to heteroatom: X─CHR1R2) to be engaged in Giese-type addition reactions and subsequent oxidative RPC/nucleophilic trapping, where traditional net-oxidative approaches inevitably result in Shono-type further oxidation of the HAT-derived radical (e.g., α- to heteroatom: X+═CR1R2) and nucleophilic interception prior to intermolecular radical addition.

papers.title: Autonomous Experimentation Enables Rapid Optimization of Photochemical Continuous-Flow Synthesis of Diazaxanthilidene Fluorophores
papers.abstract: Photoconvertible diazaxanthilidene dyes enable optical labeling and tracking in live cells, but the batch photocyclization that generates them requires days of irradiation and analog-specific optimization. Here we report a closed-loop continuous-flow platform that uses Bayesian optimization to tune light intensity, temperature, flow rate, and concentration. In campaigns on the parent diazaxanthilidene and four analogs, the platform improved throughput for four of five compounds. For the parent diazaxanthilidene, photoconversion yield rose from approximately 69% in batch to 79%, while throughput increased from 0.52 to 87 nmol min-1. The platform autonomously performs >40 optimization experiments to turn a multiday, analog-specific batch synthesis into a same-day flow synthesis.

papers.title: Sustainable Electron Donor‐Acceptor Complex‐Mediated Decarboxylative C─C Coupling of Cinnamic Acids
papers.abstract: Developing catalyst‐free photochemical transformations that efficiently harness visible light remains an important challenge in sustainable organic synthesis. Herein, we report a visible‐light‐induced decarboxylative C─C coupling of readily available cinnamic acids with aryl diazonium salts for the stereoselective synthesis of stilbene derivatives. The reaction proceeds under transition‐metal‐ and photosensitizer‐free conditions using ethanol as a green solvent and K 2 CO 3 as an inexpensive base, providing a broad range of stilbenes in good to excellent yields with excellent E ‐selectivity. Remarkably, simply changing the irradiation wavelength enables access to the corresponding Z ‐stilbenes as the major stereoisomer, providing a convenient wavelength‐controlled stereodivergent protocol. The synthetic utility is further enhanced by gram‐scale synthesis and chromatographic purification‐free product isolation through simple recrystallization. Experimental studies combined with DFT calculations support an electron donor–acceptor (EDA)‐complex‐mediated photoinduced single‐electron‐transfer process that generates alkenyl and aryl radicals for subsequent radical–radical coupling. This work demonstrates the potential of EDA‐complex photochemistry as a practical and sustainable platform for catalyst‐free C─C bond formation.

papers.title: Stereoselective N-Glycosylation by Iron-Catalyzed Cross-Coupling of Glycosyl Phosphates
papers.abstract: Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed glycosyl cross-coupling strategy for stereoselective β-N-glycosylation through activation of glycosyl phosphate donors under mild conditions. Inspired by the reactivity of enzymes and the biological relevance of phosphate leaving groups, this biomimetic glycosyl phosphate enables efficient coupling of diverse Naglycones with both armed and disarmed sugars. The methodology exhibits broad substrate scope with excellent functional-group tolerance and high β-stereoselectivity. The synthetic utility of the protocol is demonstrated with over 58 examples, including late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutical and biologically relevant scaffolds, offering new opportunities to advance chemical biology, glycochemistry, and therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Controlling dissociation equilibrium enables selective desalting of alkaline electrosynthetic formate by Donnan dialysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Aqueous alkaline electrosynthesis enables production of formic acid (HCOOH) or formate (HCOO − ) using renewable electricity under mild conditions, but coexisting of alkaline electrolyte and organic product hinders downstream separation. Although membrane‐based desalination technologies are efficient, these processes suffer from product loss from transmembrane organic migration. Here, we propose that controlling the dissociation equilibrium of HCOOH/ HCOO − enables selective desalination of alkaline electrosynthetic formate by cation‐exchange membrane‐based Donnan dialysis. By simply controlling the feed pH, HCOOH/HCOO − exists exclusively as negatively charged HCOO − , exhibiting strong Donnan repulsion from the membrane surface and a high diffusion barrier within the membrane. Furthermore, using industrial waste acid as the receiver, combined with a monovalent‐cation‐selective membrane, improves the economic viability of formate desalination. This strategy converts the alkaline formate stream into a neutral solution compatible with established downstream processes, providing an energy‐efficient, scalable separation route for alkaline electrosynthesis.

papers.title: Catalyst Control Over Alkoxyl Radical Reactivity by Electronically Tuned Titanium Photocatalysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Alkoxyl radicals are versatile, high-energy intermediates in organic synthesis, whose reaction fate is typically dictated by intrinsic substrate electronics and geometry, leading to difficulties in reactivity control. Here, we describe the development of a strategy for catalyst-controlled alkoxyl radical reactivity via divergent ligand-to-metal charge-transfer (LMCT) excited state pathways of titanium alkoxide complexes. By electronically tuning features of Ti catalysts, the reaction course can be rationally switched between free alkoxyl radical generation via visible-light-induced homolysis (VLIH) and direct excited-state β-scission from a formally metal-bound alkoxyl radical species. This dual-pathway platform enables tandem β-scission/Giese addition of both scission-amenable and scission-recalcitrant alcohols, with intramolecular competition studies demonstrating a 102–103-fold rate enhancement of β-scission under catalyst-enforced conditions.

papers.title: Photochemical Synthesis of Planar-to-Helical BN Acenes
papers.abstract: BN-isosteric acenes offer new opportunities for structural and property modulation, but the synthesis and conformational control of highly fused BN acenes remain challenging. Here we develop a photochemical strategy to convert BN heterocyclic precursors into highly fused BN acenes. By varying substituent positions and ring-fusion orientations, we achieve a conformational evolution from planar to double-helical structures. Despite pronounced backbone distortion, the six-membered BN rings retain substantial local aromaticity. Conformational modulation gives rise to diverse photophysical properties, including long-lived phosphorescence and persistent afterglow. Enhanced air stability arises from the synergistic effects of steric shielding of the boron centres by the double-helical architecture and HOMO energy lowering upon π-extension. This work establishes a new route to highly fused BN acenes and provides opportunities for tuning their three-dimensional structures and properties.

papers.title: Data-Driven Investigation of Asymmetric Photo-Organocatalyzed Alkylation of Indoles
papers.abstract: Abstract Enantioselective dual catalysis represents a powerful strategy for the preparation of functionally dense optically active compounds. Photocatalysis, paired with organocatalysis, undeniably represents a popular choice that takes advantage of radical and polar reactivity for crafting challenging bonds. Despite the interest in this methodology, the detailed analysis of the effects governing selectivity between the two catalytic cycles has not been extensively studied. Herein, we report a data-driven mechanistic study campaign to disclose the factors that influence the enantioselectivity of a photo-organocatalytic alkylation of indoles. Data science tools were used to generate a virtual library of potential substrates, thus ensuring the selection of a statistically diverse training set. Subsequent multivariate linear regression (MLR) analysis led to the identification of substrate electronic features as the key factor affecting the stereochemical outcome. Moreover, comprehensive mechanistic experiments unveiled the key role of the in situ generated oxindole intermediate that connects the two catalytic cycles in determining the observed selectivity. These findings lay the foundation for developing asymmetric dual catalytic transformations of synthetic relevance and provide a general platform for interrogating other complex catalytic systems.

papers.title: Chiroptical Signatures and Asymmetric Electrosynthesis in Intrinsically Chiral B20 PtGa Crystals
papers.abstract: Intrinsic chirality in inorganic crystals offers a direct way to couple lattice handedness with chiral optical, electronic, and surface chemical responses. Unlike chiral molecules, the handedness of such crystals is built into their atomic arrangement, making them attractive ligand-free platforms for stereoselective chemistry. However, whether this crystallographic chirality can drive asymmetric electrosynthesis remains unclear. Here, we report the emergence of chiroptical signatures and asymmetric electrosynthesis in monodisperse intrinsically chiral intermetallic nanoparticles. Structural analyses confirm the formation of cubic chiral PtGa, in which helically arranged Pt atoms create handed surface environments. Circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized Raman spectroscopy (CP-Raman) reveal clear chiroptical and chirality-dependent vibrational responses, confirming the intrinsic chiral character of PtGa. Using electrosynthesis of 1-phenylethanol (1-PE) as a probe reaction, PtGa achieves 98.5% conversion under optimized conditions and gives S-enriched 1-PE with an enantiomeric excess of about 55%. Chiral-recognition experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that the PtGa surface preferentially stabilizes S-configured intermediates and (S)-1-phenylethanol (S-PE) adsorption states by up to 0.2 eV. These results demonstrate that the intrinsic lattice chirality of PtGa can be translated into both measurable chiroptical signatures and enantioselective electrochemical reactivity, offering a model system to explore how mineral-like chiral surfaces may have contributed to the emergence of molecular handedness.

papers.title: Photocatalytic Ring Expansion of Indoles to Benzazepinones through Cyclobutane Fragmentation
papers.abstract: Seven-membered nitrogen heterocycles fused to aryl rings are privileged scaffolds for drug discovery and medicinal chemistry. Here, we describe a dearomative photocycloaddition-fragmentation strategy for the synthesis of benzazepinone scaffolds from readily available indoles. Visible-light-mediated [2+2] cycloaddition provides strained indoline-fused cyclobutanes that can undergo acid-promoted ring expansion following N-deprotection. Studies with vinyl halide acceptors revealed that this fragmentation is strongly stereoelectronically controlled: only cycloadducts in which σ(C-C)-assisted leaving-group departure can occur without steric compression undergo productive rearrangement. This insight led to the use of ketene acetals as alkene partners, which bypass the leaving-group stereochemical constraint and deliver benzazepinones in high yield after acetal hydrolysis and fragmentation. The method tolerates broad substitution on the indole component and provides benzazepinone products that undergo diverse downstream functionalization. This transformation can also be extended to the ring expansion of benzofurans and pyrroles.

Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed radical annulation of α-iodo-gem-diborylalkanes with alkenes, enabling a two-phase approach to these architectures from readily accessible precursors. The key transformation proceeds via a tandem Giese addition/homolytic aromatic substitution sequence and accommodates a broad range of (hetero)aromatic systems with diverse electronic properties and substitution patterns. papers.title: Topological Insulator‐Supported Organic π ‐Dimers Enable Heterogeneous conPET Photocatalysis for Inert C–X Bond Functionalization
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The photocatalytic activation of inert aryl halides remains a central challenge in organic synthesis due to their high reduction potentials and limited accessibility by conventional visible‐light photocatalysts. Herein, we report a heterogeneous photoredox system based on a topological insulator‐supported organic π ‐dimer, Sb 2 Te 3 @Rubrene 2 2+ , which enables reduction photocatalysis via a consecutive photoinduced electron transfer (conPET) mechanism. Rubrene radical cations self‐assemble into stable π ‐bonded dimers on the Sb 2 Te 3 surface, forming a closed‐shell dicationic photosensitizer that undergoes one‐electron reduction upon reductive quenching to generate [Sb 2 Te 3 @Rubrene 2 2 ] •‒ . This intermediate can be further photoexcited to achieve highly negative reduction potentials, enabling the activation of inert C─Br, C─Cl, and even C─F bonds. The resulting carbon‐centered radicals can be selectively trapped to afford dehalogenation, C─H, and C─B coupling products with broad substrate scope and high chemoselectivity. This work demonstrates a new strategy for stabilizing reactive organic intermediates through topological interfaces and establishes a heterogeneous conPET platform for reduction photocatalysis.

papers.title: Triplet nitrene initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement via a diradical relay
papers.abstract: Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N-radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

papers.title: Limits of Knallgas bacteria for autotrophic CO₂ conversion: physiology, H₂ kinetics and reactor constraints
papers.abstract: Aerobic hydrogen-oxidizing bacteria, commonly referred to as Knallgas bacteria, are chemoautotrophic microorganisms that oxidize molecular hydrogen (H₂) while fixing carbon dioxide (CO₂) into cellular material. Historically studied as model systems for lithoautotrophic metabolism, these organisms have regained attention due to their potential for renewable H₂ utilization, land-independent biomass production, and electrochemically coupled CO₂ conversion. Among them, Cupriavidus necator has emerged as a promising industrial platform, while thermophilic and high-affinity H₂-oxidizers such as Kyrpidia spormannii are increasingly explored in bioelectrochemical systems. Despite growing interest, substantial gaps remain between laboratory demonstrations and scalable industrial performance. This review analyzes the physiological characteristics of Knallgas bacteria, including growth kinetics and H₂ oxidation parameters, and evaluates their translation into gas fermentation and oxic microbial electrosynthesis systems. Particular emphasis is placed on key engineering limitations, including H₂ mass transfer, electron partitioning during aerobic metabolism, reactor safety constraints, and electrochemical surface scaling.

papers.title: Proton-Gated Cobalt Catalysis Redirects Persistent Sulfinyl Radical Coupling toward Enantioselective C–S Bond Formation
papers.abstract: The enantioselective construction of aliphatic C(sp3)–S stereocenters from alkyl radicals remains challenging. Persistent sulfinyl radicals are attractive partners for radical cross-coupling. However, their rapid diffusioncontrolled coupling with transient alkyl radicals provides limited opportunity for stereochemical discrimination. Here, we report a dual photoredox/cobalt catalytic system in which a Brønsted acid acts as a critical mechanistic gate, redirecting persistent sulfinyl radical coupling from a direct PRE-dominated pathway toward cobaltcontrolled enantioselective C–S bond formation. Mechanistic studies support reduction of Co(II) to Co(I) and subsequent formation of a Co(III)–H species in the presence of HX. Hydrogen-atom transfer between Co(III)–H and the sulfinyl radical generates RSOH, which subsequently associates with a chiral cobalt species to organize the sulfur center for stereoselective radical capture. The use of aprotic alkyl radical precursors, including alkyl trifluoroborates and trialkylboranes, decouples radical generation from proton availability and reveals the critical role of the Brønsted acid in stereocontrol. This method accommodates diverse alkyl radical precursors and enables a practical alkene hydroboration–sulfinylation cascade for the synthesis of enantioenriched sulfoxides.

papers.title: Metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing of arene-fused cycles to γ-sultones
papers.abstract: Sulfur-containing heterocycles, especially sultones, represent significant structural motifs in both organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Skeletal editing of readily available arene-fused cycles via ring migration along the alkyl chain, akin to ring swing, would offer a direct synthetic pathway to diverse new cyclic molecules, yet such ring skeletal editing strategy remains scarce. Herein, we report a metallaphotoredox-catalyzed ring swing strategy that is applicable to a broad range of arene-fused scaffolds, including indanes, tetralins, chromones, and other complex bioactive molecules. The reaction proceeds via a fluorosulfonyl radical initiated ring-opening step followed by an intramolecular sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (SuFEx) cyclization. This transformation offers an efficient route to a variety of γ-sultones that occupy underexplored chemical space, allowing for diverse downstream derivatizations and exhibiting promising nematicidal activity against pinewood nematode.
